content.content:
1	# Development guide
2	
3	This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
4	synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
5	Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
6	bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
7	archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
8	the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
9	Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
10	still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
11	never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
12	archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
13	preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
14	the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
15	Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
16	single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
17	The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
18	absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
19	UX-06 adds one durable local
20	sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
21	filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
22	keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.
23	
24	## Layout
25	
26	| Path | Owner |
27	|---|---|
28	| `crates/mail-core/` | Rust DTOs, fixture core, Gmail provider/auth/cache/sync/actions, SQLite, profile locks |
29	| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
30	| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |
31	| `src-tauri/` | Thin Tauri 2 shell: typed mail/draft/close commands, `mailbox_changed` and `drafts_changed` hints, fixture/Gmail profile selection and lifecycle |
32	| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |
33	
34	## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail
35	
36	The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
37	a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
38	and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
39	not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
40	25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
41	The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
42	mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
43	context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.
44	
45	Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
46	`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
47	account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
48	identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
49	A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
50	(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
51	history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
52	timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
53	an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.
54	
55	Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
56	The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
57	in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
58	and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto
59	`b4972ee`, the UX-06/07/08 contracts are preserved but not extended by this
60	increment. See [the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)
61	for evidence and remaining gates.
62	
63	## Tooling
64	
65	All commands run through [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) (pinned: node 24.4.1,
66	pnpm 10.18.0, rust 1.89.0). First-time setup:
67	
68	```sh
69	mise trust           # after inspecting the repository's mise.toml
70	mise install         # install the project-pinned runtimes/tools
71	mise run setup:linux  # Debian/Ubuntu VMs only; installs OS packages with apt-get
72	mise run install:ui   # locked frontend dependencies (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile)
73	```
74	
75	Rust dependencies resolve via the committed `Cargo.lock` on first `cargo`/`mise` use;
76	no global configuration is needed.
77	
78	### Local-only `mise.local.toml`
79	
80	`mise.local.toml` is **gitignored and machine-local** (`/mise.local.toml` in `.gitignore`):
81	it holds no secrets and must never be committed. Create it in every checkout/worktree you
82	use, with this canonical content:
83	
84	```toml
85	# Local-only launcher; OAuth credentials live outside this repository.
86	[tools]
87	# Hermetic Python provider for the dev:gmail shim (no system python3 needed).
88	uv = "0.13.7"
89	
90	[env]
91	# Stable local code-signing identity for the tauri dev binary. Without this,
92	# every rebuild is ad-hoc signed and the macOS keychain "Always Allow" grant
93	# for the mail-core-gmail item no longer matches, re-triggering the prompt.
94	APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY = "email-os-dev"
95	
96	[tasks."dev:gmail"]
97	description = "Run native Gmail mode using the private local Desktop OAuth client"
98	run = 'uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py"'
99	```
100	
101	Why each piece:
102	
103	- **`[tools] uv`** — pins uv (installed by `mise install`). The `dev:gmail` task runs its
104	  shim via `uv run --no-project`, so no system `python3` is needed, no project venv is
105	  created, and the stdlib-only shim runs on a uv-managed CPython. Bump the pin when you
106	  want a newer uv (`0.13.7` is the current latest).
107	- **`[tasks."dev:gmail"]`** — runs `~/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py`, which loads the
108	  Desktop OAuth client from `~/.config/email-os/google-desktop-client.json` (outside the
109	  repo), validates the expected `project_id`, exports `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail` plus the
110	  client env vars, and execs `mise run dev:native`. It never prints the client secret.
111	  Validate the config without launching the app or making any Google request:
112	  `mise x -- uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py" --check`
113	- **`[env] APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`** (macOS only) — without this, the tauri dev binary is
114	  ad-hoc signed and every `cargo` rebuild changes its signature; keychain "Always Allow"
115	  grants are tied to the code signature, so the `mail-core-gmail` keychain prompt reappears
116	  on every `mise run dev:gmail`. Signing the dev binary with a stable local certificate
117	  keeps a single grant across rebuilds.
118	
119	One-time macOS keychain setup:
120	
121	1. **Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Create a Certificate**: name it
122	   `email-os-dev`, identity type *Self Signed Root*, certificate type **Code Signing**
123	   (default validity 1 year; recreate with the same name when it expires, then re-allow
124	   once).
125	2. Run `mise run dev:gmail` once and click **Always Allow** on the "email-os wants to use
126	   your confidential information stored in `mail-core-gmail`" prompt. The grant is pinned
127	   to the `email-os-dev` identity, so rebuilds no longer prompt.
128	3. Do **not** set the keychain item's Access Control to "Allow all applications to access
129	   this item" — that silences the prompt forever but lets *any* app running as you read
130	   the Gmail tokens silently. Keep the per-app grant.
131	
132	The stored token is one keychain generic-password entry (service `mail-core-gmail`,
133	account `single-profile`, `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` — local, not synced to iCloud).
134	To rotate/disconnect, delete it (`security delete-generic-password -s mail-core-gmail -a
135	single-profile`) or use the app's disconnect action; the next `mise run dev:gmail` starts
136	a fresh OAuth flow. Never paste credentials into the app, logs, screenshots, or reports.
137	
138	## Validation gates
139	
140	Core and frontend gates run independently of native GTK/WebKit prerequisites:
141	
142	| Task | What it does |
143	|---|---|
144	| `mise run check` | Core tests, generated-contract check, core lint, UI tests and typecheck |
145	| `mise run test:core` | `cargo test -p mail-core` — synthetic fixture and Gmail auth/cache/sync tests; no real accounts or Google network |
146	| `mise run check:contract` | Regenerates the TS wire contract to a temp file and **fails on drift** against `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` |
147	| `mise run gen:ts` | Regenerates `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` from Rust DTOs |
148	| `mise run lint:core` | Workspace formatting and `clippy -D warnings` for mail-core |
149	| `mise run test:ui` | Vitest component/transport tests |
150	| `mise run typecheck` | `vue-tsc --noEmit` |
151	| `mise run build:web` | Frontend production build to `dist/` |
152	| `mise run check:native` | Locked compile-check of the Tauri shell and native tests |
153	| `mise run test:native` | Native shell bridge tests |
154	| `mise run dev:native` | Tauri dev app; GTK/WebKit development packages are required on Linux |
155	| `mise run build:native` | Bundled native app |
156	
157	## Running the app
158	
159	**Browser preview (in-memory, not durable):** `mise run dev:web`, then open the
160	printed localhost URL. UX-13A mounts two explicitly synthetic **in-app account
161	workspaces**, each with its own labelled in-memory client and the same conversation
162	IDs. These are not native tabs. Switch with the account buttons or the supported
163	Switch account command; the current local editor must save/recover successfully
164	before leaving. Each workspace retains navigation/Back, selection, command query,
165	reader state, focus and scroll. There is no mail-search capability on this UX-05
166	base (UX-06/07 are absent), real OAuth, credentials or mailbox access in preview.
167	Native mode remains a single account/window and exposes no switch command. See
168	[UX-13A's contract and remaining gates](ux-13-independent-workspaces.md).
169	
170	**Native fixture mode (default):** `mise run dev:native`. This opens the synthetic
171	fixture profile under `<app_data_dir>/fixture-profile`; local drafts are stored
172	separately beneath `<app_data_dir>/fixture-profile/local-drafts`. The fixture
173	provider's optional demo behavior is selected with
174	`EMAIL_OS_FAKE_PROVIDER=paused|reject|success` (default: success). Profile locks
175	reject a second writer to the same mail or draft profile.
176	
177	**Explicit native Gmail mode:** launch with `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail`; it uses the
178	separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile`, never the fixture database. Local drafts
179	are in the separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile/local-drafts` profile; disconnect
180	retains those drafts on this device for the same account after reconnect. Set the
181	Google client environment before launching:
182	
183	```sh
184	EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail \
185	EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID='your-desktop-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com' \
186	EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET='optional-desktop-client-secret' \
187	mise run dev:native
188	```
189	
190	The client secret is optional. It belongs only in the local launch environment,
191	not source control, frontend state, logs, or a shell history copied into a report.
192	Initial connection requests only `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`.
193	Missing/blank client ID shows `Not configured` in Gmail mode; it does not fail app
194	startup or fall back to the fixture. Unsupported Keychain platforms fail closed.
195	Mailbox controls stay disabled until the user selects **Enable mailbox actions**
196	and Google returns a verified modify grant for the same authenticated account.
197	That upgrade requests `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify`; Google's
198	scope is broader than this app's implemented archive/unarchive and read/unread
199	commands and can authorize other mailbox changes (including sending or deleting
200	mail). The app does not provide those broader actions, arbitrary labels, or a
201	composer. Denial or cancellation leaves the read-only account and cached reading
202	available.
203	
204	### Google Desktop OAuth setup (disposable account only)
205	
206	For the explicitly approved Mac smoke path, use a dedicated Google Cloud project
207	and disposable Gmail account, not a primary/personal mailbox:
208	
209	1. Enable the **Gmail API** in the project.
210	2. Configure the OAuth consent screen and add the disposable account as a test
211	   user when the app is in **Testing** status.
212	3. Create an OAuth client of type **Desktop app**. Put its client ID in
213	   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`; the optional client secret goes only in
214	   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in the launch environment.
215	4. Confirm initial connection requests only `gmail.readonly`. The separate
216	   **Enable mailbox actions** flow requests Google's broader `gmail.modify` scope
217	   only after explicit user opt-in; do not add any other Gmail scopes.
218	5. On first use, review the macOS Keychain access prompt and allow the app to use
219	   its Gmail credential item. Credential-storage failures are visible and fail
220	   closed; there is no plaintext fallback.
221	
222	Google OAuth clients left in Testing can issue refresh tokens that expire after
223	seven days for these Gmail scopes. Plan for a fresh sign-in during testing; this
224	is not a reason to log or persist tokens elsewhere. A terminal-launched Tauri
225	process inherits that terminal's environment. Finder-launched apps generally do
226	not inherit the shell's exported variables; if configuration appears missing,
227	use the documented launch environment for the app rather than silently selecting
228	fixture mode. Never paste secrets into the UI or a bug report.
229	
230	Disconnect removes credentials from this app's Keychain item and clears the
231	local Gmail profile/cache. It is a **local disconnect**, not a promise to revoke
232	the Google grant or revoke tokens remotely; revoke authorization through the
233	Google account controls separately if required.
234	
235	### Gmail sync pacing and rate limits
236	
237	The disposable-account diagnostic observed HTTP 403 `rateLimitExceeded` after
238	~60 rapid thread reads, so discovery is paced for read-only Gmail quotas:
239	`threads.list` discovery pages request 25 threads (the overall disclosed cap
240	stays 100 conversations), consecutive Gmail API reads are separated by a
241	100 ms minimum interval whose wait aborts promptly on cancellation, and a
242	mid-page failure commits the threads already fetched (the page token is not
243	advanced), so a rate-limit retry or restart resumes from durable progress
244	instead of re-fetching saved threads. HTTP 403 is classified by bounded
245	structured Google error reasons: only genuine quota rejections (e.g.
246	`rateLimitExceeded`, `userRateLimitExceeded`, `dailyLimitExceeded`,
247	`quotaExceeded`, `resourceExhausted`) surface as `rate_limited`; permission
248	denials and unclassifiable bodies surface as the generic provider error. Raw
249	response bodies, messages, mailbox data, or URLs with IDs are never logged or
250	exposed over IPC.
251	
252	### Disposable Mac smoke checklist (Slice 02 prior operator validation)
253	
254	Run only on the operator-approved disposable-account Mac path:
255	
256	- Verify fixture is the default, `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail` is explicit, and missing
257	  client ID reports `Not configured` without fixture rows.
258	- Connect, complete the system-browser OAuth/loopback callback, cancel once, and
259	  verify cancellation is recoverable; confirm Keychain credentials survive an
260	  app restart without exposing them.
261	- Complete bounded initial discovery, inspect plain-text content and unsupported
262	  content disclosures, and verify archive controls/shortcuts remain absent until
263	  the separate explicit Slice 03 permission upgrade is enabled.
264	- Quit, disable network, relaunch, and read cached conversations offline; restore
265	  network and sync. Change/archive/delete a thread using the external disposable
266	  Gmail client and confirm catch-up updates the local inbox without skipping the
267	  expired-cursor recovery path.
268	- Disconnect and confirm local cache/credentials are cleared while understanding
269	  that Google authorization itself is not remotely revoked.
270	
271	No real-account OAuth, Gmail network, or macOS Keychain behavior was tested in the
272	Linux integration VM. The operator's earlier Slice 01 validation and prior Slice 02
273	Mac validation are separate gates; neither substitutes for the new Slice 03
274	consent, mutation, recovery, and external-change checks.
275	
276	### Mailbox-action validation (Slice 03 still pending on Mac)
277	
278	Run this only after the separate Slice 02 disposable-account checks, on the
279	operator-approved disposable Mac account. Keep Gmail read-only until the explicit
280	upgrade button is chosen. Verify both grant and deny/cancel paths:
281	
282	- On the read-only account, verify cached reading still works and opening a
283	  conversation does not mark it read. Request **Enable mailbox actions** only
284	  after reviewing the broader `gmail.modify` scope disclosure. Confirm the UI
285	  remains read-only/upgrading until authoritative account status reports a
286	  verified same-account grant. Deny OAuth and cancel an in-progress upgrade in
287	  separate runs; each must retain the old read credential, cache and reading
288	  access without reporting actions enabled. Upgrade cancellation is not
289	  disconnect and must not revoke a completed Google grant.
290	- With actions enabled, explicitly archive a conversation, then explicitly
291	  mark it read and unread. Confirm Activity distinguishes queued, applying,
292	  confirmed, failed and outcome-unknown; verify ordinary opening does not alter
293	  read state. Disconnect warning must explain that local pending operations are
294	  removed but confirmed remote Gmail changes are not undone and Google's grant
295	  is not revoked.
296	- Queue an archive while offline, restart, restore network, and verify durable
297	  Activity/recovery. Interrupted setter dispatch must be reconciled with a GET
298	  over its exact original message IDs before confirmation; it must not
299	  automatically POST again. A newer incoming message must not be added to an
300	  older operation's target snapshot. Use explicit Retry only for a failed or
301	  outcome-unknown operation and verify it creates a new request ID while
302	  retaining the old immutable targets; a retry can override the current state.
303	- Archive enough conversations to exercise the 100-conversation view cap,
304	  restart, and recover an archived conversation from Activity. The reader must
305	  identify a retained local recovery snapshot and warn Gmail may have newer
306	  messages or mailbox changes. Make an external archive/read change in the
307	  disposable Gmail client, sync, and verify provider facts update without
308	  erasing a newer pending local intent.
309	
310	The Slice 03 provider, persistence, bridge and browser behavior is covered with
311	synthetic HTTP/fake-provider tests only in this VM. This new Mac checkpoint is
312	not satisfied by the operator's earlier Slice 02 validation; OAuth consent,
313	Keychain upgrades, native command registration and all Slice 03 scenarios remain
314	pending operator validation.
315	
316	### Local drafts and normal close (Slice 04)
317	
318	Native `list_drafts`, `get_draft`, `create_draft`, `save_draft`, and
319	`delete_draft` commands use a dedicated `local-drafts/drafts.db` with its own
320	profile lock and FULL/WAL transactions. The bridge derives account scope from
321	backend status rather than an account ID supplied by the UI; local drafts do not
322	require Gmail's `gmail.modify` permission. Disconnect retains local drafts,
323	but disconnect clears cached account identity, so native list/edit access resumes
324	after reconnecting the same account. Drafts from another account are never
325	returned by the selected account's commands.
326	
327	Draft To/Cc/subject/body text is stored exactly as entered, including incomplete
328	recipients, whitespace and Unicode. Limits are 16 KiB each for To and Cc, 4 KiB
329	for subject, and 1 MiB for body; oversized values fail instead of truncating or
330	normalizing. This is local editor storage, not recipient validation or send
331	readiness. Revisions start at 1; save/discard use expected-revision checks.
332	Exact request retries return durable receipts; conflicting reuse of a key is
333	rejected. Receipts/tombstones do not store body content, and deletes do not let
334	late saves resurrect a draft. Only a committed receipt is a durable saved label.
335	
336	Reply is only available for the explicitly selected latest message with complete
337	current non-retained plaintext and trustworthy metadata. A single From mailbox
338	is required. Absent Reply-To falls back to From; malformed, empty, group, or
339	ambiguous Reply-To fails closed. Display names do not expand, aliases and
340	plus/dot equivalence are not inferred, duplicate mailboxes are removed, and the
341	account's primary mailbox is excluded. Reply to the account's own latest sent
342	message is unsupported. A reply starts with empty Cc/body and one `Re:` prefix;
343	there is no reply-all, Bcc, signature, or automatic quoted text. Legacy cache
344	rows can use a readonly metadata-only Gmail fetch when online; cached metadata
345	hits are network-free. If that metadata is unavailable offline, reply preparation
346	is unavailable, while new-message and existing-draft editing remain local.
347	
348	Native window Close and normal OS quit pause behind an in-memory
349	`app_close_requested` request. The UI flushes the current buffer, then completes
350	only that request after a durable receipt; failure/conflict cancels the request
351	and leaves the window and buffer open. Requests coalesce, stale IDs are rejected,
352	and completion without a pending native request cannot close the app. Browser
353	preview only models this protocol in memory and is never durable. Force quit,
354	crash, or power loss before a save ACK is not guaranteed to preserve the latest
355	keystrokes.
356	
357	### Disposable Mac smoke checklist (Slice 04 pending)
358	
359	Run only after the existing Slice 02 and Slice 03 operator checkpoints, using a
360	disposable Mac/profile and no production account:
361	
362	- Edit recipient, subject, and body immediately before normal window Close and
363	  Cmd+Q in separate runs; restart and verify exact committed recovery.
364	- Inject a save failure and a stale-revision conflict during close; verify the
365	  app stays open, the buffer remains exact, the request is cancelled, and no
366	  saved label appears without a committed receipt.
367	- Verify cached/offline, readonly, and auth-expired editing needs no Gmail modify
368	  grant. Verify a legacy first Reply uses only the readonly metadata enrichment
369	  path when available.
370	- Disconnect/reconnect the same account and verify drafts remain on this device;
371	  switch account and verify no cross-account draft visibility or mutation.
372	- After reply creation evict/retain the source conversation and verify the
373	  immutable reply link survives while stale, retained, incomplete, or unsupported
374	  source preparation fails closed.
375	- Exercise idempotent retry, duplicate create before metadata reads, delete versus
376	  late save, and verify no send/outbox/provider-draft side effect.
377	- Verify fixture native restart recovery and that browser preview continues to
378	  label its memory-only drafts as non-durable.
379	
380	Slice 04 synthetic core/UI checks pass in this VM. Native Tauri compile-check
381	currently stops at the missing `pkg-config`/GTK prerequisites described below;
382	no OS packages were installed. Native close handling and this Mac checkpoint
383	remain pending operator validation.
384	
385	### Safe bulk selection and processing (UX-05)
386	
387	Conversations can be selected in the Inbox/Done list with `X`, `Shift+J/K`,
388	Cmd/Ctrl-click, Shift-click ranges and per-row labelled checkboxes, bounded to
389	100 selected conversations per action (additive ranges; Select all loaded is
390	disabled with an explanation beyond the bound; selection clears on
391	context/account changes and survives reader visits with a visible bulk-scope
392	banner). Shared toolbar, palette and shortcut actions apply to the whole
393	selection when one exists (group path, even for one row); inline row actions
394	stay row-scoped, and Reply/open/navigation are never bulk.
395	
396	A bulk action accepts one durable **operation group**: structure, duplicates,
397	bounds, request ID, active account and capability are validated before a single
398	SQLite transaction persists the group header, immutable per-member targets and
399	preimages, and per-member acceptance results. A gone/unactionable member becomes
400	a persisted typed rejection, not a fabricated failed provider operation;
401	all-rejected valid requests get an idempotent receipt and consume no Undo slot.
402	Same-request replays (including after restart) return the original receipt;
403	changed payloads are `request_id_conflict`. Archive/unarchive groups work in
404	fixture and Gmail mode; read/unread groups are Gmail-only, like the single
405	setters.
406	
407	`Z` within the 10-second Rust-clock window undoes the latest top-level action,
408	whether a single or a group. A group Undo makes one durable attempt: queued
409	members are cancelled, applying/confirmed members are compensated from the
410	original preimages, and ineligible members (failed, unknown outcome, unknown
411	prior, already undone, acceptance-rejected) are explicitly skipped with reasons.
412	Partial results are worded honestly: the dock line stays short ("Restored 1 · 1
413	skipped — failed"; skips are named only when there are some) while its title and
414	accessible description keep the exact ledger ("Undo accepted for 1 of 2; 1
415	skipped (1 failed); …"), and per-member failures stay recoverable in Activity regardless of
416	current list rows. A rejected IPC acceptance is never treated as "nothing
417	happened": the UI keeps the original request ID and recovers via
418	`get_operation_group` / replay of the exact original request.
419	
420	Browser-preview group behavior is modelled by the labelled in-memory fake, which
421	continues to disclose that it is non-durable; it makes no provider or storage
422	calls.
423	
424	#### Disposable Mac smoke checklist (UX-05 pending)
425	
426	Run only on the operator-approved disposable Mac path, after the Slice 02–04
427	checkpoints: actual `X`/`Shift+J`/`Shift+K`/Cmd-Shift-click selection and
428	clear/last-row focus, Escape clearing selection before leaving a context,
429	bulk Done/read against the fixture or disposable account, `Z` group Undo inside
430	and outside the window, restart recovery of group receipts and Activity members,
431	and VoiceOver selection/outcome announcements. Native IPC command registration
432	is covered only by the bridge tests in this VM; Gmail read-group remote
433	convergence (BROWSE-18) additionally requires the approved disposable account.
434	
435	## UX-10 A — Read-only cached Trash (partial UX-10)
436	
437	Gmail mode exposes **Go to cached Trash (read only)** in Commands and Destinations.
438	This lists known locally cached TRASH conversations, including operation-retained
439	snapshots; it does not discover Gmail Trash or claim mailbox-complete coverage.
440	Refresh is explicit, pagination is bounded, and Back preserves the loaded local
441	browsing state. Trash-origin readers omit mailbox actions and Reply. Opening
442	never marks read. The native fixture profile rejects this Gmail-only query;
443	browser-preview fixtures can simulate it in memory.
444	
445	Observed per-message TRASH/SPAM facts now exclude those conversations from Inbox
446	and Done. Old profiles migrate with unknown (nullable) triage facts; unknown is
447	not asserted to be outside Trash/Spam. No mutation permission or provider write
448	was added. Existing archive/read durable intent, groups, Undo, Activity, local
449	drafts and close protections remain in place.
450	
451	See [UX-10 bounded contracts and acceptance](ux-10-bounded-triage.md). Trash/recover
452	writes and Undo await a recovery-effects decision and a new durable dimension;
453	mute/spam writes, Important/Other, rules, Block and Unsubscribe are not enabled.
454	There is no permanent-delete/empty-Trash, arbitrary URL opener or send command.
455	Synthetic checks do not establish native WKWebView or remote Gmail convergence.
456	## UX-12 attachment capability and validation
457	
458	See [UX-12 contract and evidence](ux-12-safe-attachments.md). The reader's Files
459	and links button (native Cmd+O) offers up to 32 cached descriptors and 32 literal
460	HTTP(S) links. No automatic read, file opening or URL dispatch occurs. Gmail
461	uses its existing readonly grant; only explicit Save issues attachment-endpoint
462	reads and decodes file bytes in Rust. Inline body-only parts without a fetchable
463	attachment ID are omitted; existing bounded full-thread reads can contain inline
464	payload fields, which are not decoded as attachments.
465	Missing/legacy descriptors need a sync; retained snapshots do not acquire new
466	provider authority. No attachment uploads, provider drafts or sending.
467	
468	Saves create a unique file directly in OS Downloads with a `.download` suffix;
469	the frontend cannot supply a destination. Files never execute and must be
470	inspected/renamed outside the app. Cancel/dismiss discards an unfinished
471	transfer (a blocked HTTP call can take its existing 30-second timeout to return);
472	a completed save or process crash may leave an inert file. A lost save response
473	may leave a completed download; retries can create another unique file. Browser
474	preview only models a memory-only save and external handoff, not filesystem or
475	provider effects. External HTTP(S) dispatch currently targets macOS only.
476	
477	PDF preview is **not implemented**: the restricted macOS platform sandbox and
478	compatibility spike has not passed. No PDF/HTML/Office document enters a webview,
479	trusted DOM or third-party viewer. Native build/bridge tests do not satisfy
480	WKWebView key handling, VoiceOver, Downloads permissions, OS browser dispatch,
481	or the PDF security spike. Disposable provider validation remains separately
482	operator-gated, not authorized by implementation work.
483	
484	## Desktop-local reminder increment (UX-11)
485	
486	See [the local reminder contract](ux-11-local-reminders.md) and
487	ADR 0001's reminder boundary. H / Remind me supports one Inbox conversation,
488	local time presets and free-text dates (or unscheduled Someday),
489	default If no reply / Regardless, and
490	Reminders pending/returned/history destinations (also G then H and palette).
491	Cancel/recover and reschedule are revisioned, durable commands. Pending stages
492	are not provider confirmation; returned membership requires confirmed return.
493	The existing fixture worker executes while running and reconciles overdue work
494	on launch. No execution while fully quit, cross-device state or calendar.
495	
496	Gmail commands use local `gmail.db` reminders, immutable baseline IDs, a pinned
497	reader snapshot, account-scoped request receipts, and revision checks. They do
498	not enqueue Gmail archive or unarchive operations. Pending Inbox hiding ends
499	when a new message ID is observed. Regardless deadlines resolve locally. A
500	no-reply deadline needs a connected, complete fresh thread read. Offline,
501	incomplete, and failed reads stay pending. A provider reply can arrive after the
502	observed checkpoint and before commit; the decision is local and is not an
503	atomic provider absence guarantee. The browser fake supports memory-only reminder transport for UI tests and
504	development. Its due transitions reconcile on synthetic reads; they do not
505	establish native persistence or worker execution.
506	No credentials or real provider were used for this increment.
507	
508	## Synthetic account workspaces (UX-13A)
509	
510	### UX-13A validation boundaries
511	
512	`tests/workspaces.component.test.ts` and `browser-fake.accounts.test.ts` exercise
513	two synthetic identities with colliding conversation/message/draft/request IDs,
514	late detail/list/action results, independent Back/focus/selection/command queries,
515	save-before-switch, failed saves and serialized pending saves. This is in-memory
516	frontend integration, not proof of native account/credential ownership.
517	
518	The existing opt-in `tests/discovery.rendered.test.ts` CDP harness also contains a
519	`UX-13:` pointer/keyboard journey (isolated temporary Chromium profile). Run with
520	`EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/path/to/chromium mise exec -- pnpm exec vitest run tests/discovery.rendered.test.ts -t 'UX-13:'`.
521	It checks actual inert focus rejection, independent IDs/selection, list scroll,
522	reader Back and exact account-local action outcomes. It does not test WKWebView
523	or native tabs. Existing core mail/Gmail/draft profile-lock tests remain the
524	exclusive-writer regression gate; frontend sessions are not native profile leases.
525	No IPC, command registration, permissions or Rust-generated TS change in UX-13A.
526	
527	Native account expansion is blocked on approval of a registry/credential/lease/
528	close-coordinator design. Current `KeychainSecrets` is a single global
529	`mail-core-gmail` / `single-profile` entry, not one credential namespace per DB
530	directory. Do not run a second Gmail profile as a multi-account workaround.
531	
532	## Native prerequisites and platform limits
533	
534	For a Debian/Ubuntu Linux VM, run the explicit setup task once:
535	
536	```sh
537	mise run setup:linux
538	```
539	
540	It runs `apt-get update`, then installs the compiler tools, `pkg-config`,
541	GTK/WebKitGTK development libraries, `librsvg2-dev`, and `dbus-daemon`. WebKitGTK
542	pulls in its Soup and JavaScriptCore dependencies. It also installs `xvfb`,
543	`xauth`, `xdotool`, `openbox`, `x11-utils`, and `scrot` for native window capture.
544	It uses `sudo` unless run as root. Re-running it keeps installed packages and
545	installs any missing ones; apt may update the listed packages.
546	
547	The task rejects non-Linux hosts and hosts without `apt-get` before any package
548	operation. Other Linux distributions need equivalent packages installed manually.
549	It does not install mise runtimes or frontend dependencies. No build, check, or
550	macOS task depends on it. Do not run OS setup as part of an integration check.
551	macOS still uses Xcode command line tools and WKWebView, with the existing local
552	signing setup above.
553	
554	### Native screenshots on a headless Linux VM
555	
556	Use synthetic fixture mode and an isolated temporary data directory. Start the
557	app in a virtual X11 desktop from the repository root:
558	
559	```sh
560	export EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/email-os-capture.XXXXXX)"
561	echo "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR"  # use this path in the second terminal
562	xvfb-run -a --server-args='-screen 0 1280x900x24 -nolisten tcp' sh -c '
563	  printf "%s\n" "$DISPLAY" > "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/display"
564	  printf "%s\n" "$XAUTHORITY" > "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/xauthority"
565	  openbox &
566	  export GDK_BACKEND=x11 EMAIL_OS_MODE=fixture
567	  export XDG_DATA_HOME="$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/data"
568	  exec dbus-run-session -- mise run dev:native
569	'
570	```
571	
572	Wait for the native window to load. In a second terminal, set the printed path:
573	
574	```sh
575	export EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/email-os-capture.XXXXXX  # replace with printed path
576	export DISPLAY="$(cat "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/display")"
577	export XAUTHORITY="$(cat "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/xauthority")"
578	xdotool windowactivate --sync "$(xdotool search --onlyvisible --class email-os | head -1)"
579	scrot -u -b "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/native-inbox.png"
580	```
581	
582	Use `xdotool` mouse/keyboard actions to open a conversation or Commands, then
583	capture another PNG. Stop the first terminal with Ctrl+C when finished. The
584	temporary directory retains the screenshots and isolated fixture data.
585	The default native task starts Vite on port 5173; free that port before launch.
586	For browser captures, run `mise run dev:web` and open its URL in the browser;
587	browser preview uses separate in-memory fixtures.
588	
589	Linux native screenshots exercise WebKitGTK and the Rust fixture backend.
590	They do not validate macOS WKWebView/IME, Keychain prompts, system browser
591	launch, loopback OAuth interaction, or Google TLS behavior. Keep those Mac gates
592	separate. No sandbox or app security setting needs to be disabled for capture.
593	
594	## Fixture data
595	
596	Fixture mode uses only synthetic `fixture-account`, `conv-01`…`conv-18` rows,
597	seeded once; it never resets provider facts or operation history. Gmail mode has a
598	separate SQLite schema/profile and bounded cache. Neither mode logs subjects,
599	addresses, bodies, OAuth codes, or credentials. Gmail history catch-up does not
600	import arbitrary newly observed archived-thread bodies; the disclosed cache is
601	limited to up to 100 discovered conversations and may omit inbox threads outside
602	the bounded view.

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

## Layout

| Path | Owner |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto
`b4972ee`, the UX-06/07/08 contracts are preserved but not extended by this
increment. See [the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)
for evidence and remaining gates.

## Tooling

All commands run through [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev) (pinned: node 24.4.1,
pnpm 10.18.0, rust 1.89.0). First-time setup:

```sh
mise trust           # after inspecting the repository's mise.toml
mise install         # install the project-pinned runtimes/tools
mise run setup:linux  # Debian/Ubuntu VMs only; installs OS packages with apt-get
mise run install:ui   # locked frontend dependencies (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile)
```

Rust dependencies resolve via the committed `Cargo.lock` on first `cargo`/`mise` use;
no global configuration is needed.

### Local-only `mise.local.toml`

`mise.local.toml` is **gitignored and machine-local** (`/mise.local.toml` in `.gitignore`):
it holds no secrets and must never be committed. Create it in every checkout/worktree you
use, with this canonical content:

```toml
# Local-only launcher; OAuth credentials live outside this repository.
[tools]
# Hermetic Python provider for the dev:gmail shim (no system python3 needed).
uv = "0.13.7"

[env]
# Stable local code-signing identity for the tauri dev binary. Without this,
# every rebuild is ad-hoc signed and the macOS keychain "Always Allow" grant
# for the mail-core-gmail item no longer matches, re-triggering the prompt.
APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY = "email-os-dev"

[tasks."dev:gmail"]
description = "Run native Gmail mode using the private local Desktop OAuth client"
run = 'uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py"'
```

Why each piece:

- **`[tools] uv`** — pins uv (installed by `mise install`). The `dev:gmail` task runs its
  shim via `uv run --no-project`, so no system `python3` is needed, no project venv is
  created, and the stdlib-only shim runs on a uv-managed CPython. Bump the pin when you
  want a newer uv (`0.13.7` is the current latest).
- **`[tasks."dev:gmail"]`** — runs `~/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py`, which loads the
  Desktop OAuth client from `~/.config/email-os/google-desktop-client.json` (outside the
  repo), validates the expected `project_id`, exports `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail` plus the
  client env vars, and execs `mise run dev:native`. It never prints the client secret.
  Validate the config without launching the app or making any Google request:
  `mise x -- uv run --no-project "$HOME/.config/email-os/dev-gmail.py" --check`
- **`[env] APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY`** (macOS only) — without this, the tauri dev binary is
  ad-hoc signed and every `cargo` rebuild changes its signature; keychain "Always Allow"
  grants are tied to the code signature, so the `mail-core-gmail` keychain prompt reappears
  on every `mise run dev:gmail`. Signing the dev binary with a stable local certificate
  keeps a single grant across rebuilds.

One-time macOS keychain setup:

1. **Keychain Access → Certificate Assistant → Create a Certificate**: name it
   `email-os-dev`, identity type *Self Signed Root*, certificate type **Code Signing**
   (default validity 1 year; recreate with the same name when it expires, then re-allow
   once).
2. Run `mise run dev:gmail` once and click **Always Allow** on the "email-os wants to use
   your confidential information stored in `mail-core-gmail`" prompt. The grant is pinned
   to the `email-os-dev` identity, so rebuilds no longer prompt.
3. Do **not** set the keychain item's Access Control to "Allow all applications to access
   this item" — that silences the prompt forever but lets *any* app running as you read
   the Gmail tokens silently. Keep the per-app grant.

The stored token is one keychain generic-password entry (service `mail-core-gmail`,
account `single-profile`, `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` — local, not synced to iCloud).
To rotate/disconnect, delete it (`security delete-generic-password -s mail-core-gmail -a
single-profile`) or use the app's disconnect action; the next `mise run dev:gmail` starts
a fresh OAuth flow. Never paste credentials into the app, logs, screenshots, or reports.

## Running the app

**Browser preview (in-memory, not durable):** `mise run dev:web`, then open the
printed localhost URL. UX-13A mounts two explicitly synthetic **in-app account
workspaces**, each with its own labelled in-memory client and the same conversation
IDs. These are not native tabs. Switch with the account buttons or the supported
Switch account command; the current local editor must save/recover successfully
before leaving. Each workspace retains navigation/Back, selection, command query,
reader state, focus and scroll. There is no mail-search capability on this UX-05
base (UX-06/07 are absent), real OAuth, credentials or mailbox access in preview.
Native mode remains a single account/window and exposes no switch command. See
[UX-13A's contract and remaining gates](ux-13-independent-workspaces.md).

**Native fixture mode (default):** `mise run dev:native`. This opens the synthetic
fixture profile under `<app_data_dir>/fixture-profile`; local drafts are stored
separately beneath `<app_data_dir>/fixture-profile/local-drafts`. The fixture
provider's optional demo behavior is selected with
`EMAIL_OS_FAKE_PROVIDER=paused|reject|success` (default: success). Profile locks
reject a second writer to the same mail or draft profile.

**Explicit native Gmail mode:** launch with `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail`; it uses the
separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile`, never the fixture database. Local drafts
are in the separate `<app_data_dir>/gmail-profile/local-drafts` profile; disconnect
retains those drafts on this device for the same account after reconnect. Set the
Google client environment before launching:

```sh
EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail \
EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID='your-desktop-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com' \
EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET='optional-desktop-client-secret' \
mise run dev:native
```

The client secret is optional. It belongs only in the local launch environment,
not source control, frontend state, logs, or a shell history copied into a report.
Initial connection requests only `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly`.
Missing/blank client ID shows `Not configured` in Gmail mode; it does not fail app
startup or fall back to the fixture. Unsupported Keychain platforms fail closed.
Mailbox controls stay disabled until the user selects **Enable mailbox actions**
and Google returns a verified modify grant for the same authenticated account.
That upgrade requests `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify`; Google's
scope is broader than this app's implemented archive/unarchive and read/unread
commands and can authorize other mailbox changes (including sending or deleting
mail). The app does not provide those broader actions, arbitrary labels, or a
composer. Denial or cancellation leaves the read-only account and cached reading
available.

### Google Desktop OAuth setup (disposable account only)

For the explicitly approved Mac smoke path, use a dedicated Google Cloud project
and disposable Gmail account, not a primary/personal mailbox:

1. Enable the **Gmail API** in the project.
2. Configure the OAuth consent screen and add the disposable account as a test
   user when the app is in **Testing** status.
3. Create an OAuth client of type **Desktop app**. Put its client ID in
   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`; the optional client secret goes only in
   `EMAIL_OS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` in the launch environment.
4. Confirm initial connection requests only `gmail.readonly`. The separate
   **Enable mailbox actions** flow requests Google's broader `gmail.modify` scope
   only after explicit user opt-in; do not add any other Gmail scopes.
5. On first use, review the macOS Keychain access prompt and allow the app to use
   its Gmail credential item. Credential-storage failures are visible and fail
   closed; there is no plaintext fallback.

Google OAuth clients left in Testing can issue refresh tokens that expire after
seven days for these Gmail scopes. Plan for a fresh sign-in during testing; this
is not a reason to log or persist tokens elsewhere. A terminal-launched Tauri
process inherits that terminal's environment. Finder-launched apps generally do
not inherit the shell's exported variables; if configuration appears missing,
use the documented launch environment for the app rather than silently selecting
fixture mode. Never paste secrets into the UI or a bug report.

Disconnect removes credentials from this app's Keychain item and clears the
local Gmail profile/cache. It is a **local disconnect**, not a promise to revoke
the Google grant or revoke tokens remotely; revoke authorization through the
Google account controls separately if required.

### Gmail sync pacing and rate limits

The disposable-account diagnostic observed HTTP 403 `rateLimitExceeded` after
~60 rapid thread reads, so discovery is paced for read-only Gmail quotas:
`threads.list` discovery pages request 25 threads (the overall disclosed cap
stays 100 conversations), consecutive Gmail API reads are separated by a
100 ms minimum interval whose wait aborts promptly on cancellation, and a
mid-page failure commits the threads already fetched (the page token is not
advanced), so a rate-limit retry or restart resumes from durable progress
instead of re-fetching saved threads. HTTP 403 is classified by bounded
structured Google error reasons: only genuine quota rejections (e.g.
`rateLimitExceeded`, `userRateLimitExceeded`, `dailyLimitExceeded`,
`quotaExceeded`, `resourceExhausted`) surface as `rate_limited`; permission
denials and unclassifiable bodies surface as the generic provider error. Raw
response bodies, messages, mailbox data, or URLs with IDs are never logged or
exposed over IPC.

### Local drafts and normal close (Slice 04)

Native `list_drafts`, `get_draft`, `create_draft`, `save_draft`, and
`delete_draft` commands use a dedicated `local-drafts/drafts.db` with its own
profile lock and FULL/WAL transactions. The bridge derives account scope from
backend status rather than an account ID supplied by the UI; local drafts do not
require Gmail's `gmail.modify` permission. Disconnect retains local drafts,
but disconnect clears cached account identity, so native list/edit access resumes
after reconnecting the same account. Drafts from another account are never
returned by the selected account's commands.

Draft To/Cc/subject/body text is stored exactly as entered, including incomplete
recipients, whitespace and Unicode. Limits are 16 KiB each for To and Cc, 4 KiB
for subject, and 1 MiB for body; oversized values fail instead of truncating or
normalizing. This is local editor storage, not recipient validation or send
readiness. Revisions start at 1; save/discard use expected-revision checks.
Exact request retries return durable receipts; conflicting reuse of a key is
rejected. Receipts/tombstones do not store body content, and deletes do not let
late saves resurrect a draft. Only a committed receipt is a durable saved label.

Reply is only available for the explicitly selected latest message with complete
current non-retained plaintext and trustworthy metadata. A single From mailbox
is required. Absent Reply-To falls back to From; malformed, empty, group, or
ambiguous Reply-To fails closed. Display names do not expand, aliases and
plus/dot equivalence are not inferred, duplicate mailboxes are removed, and the
account's primary mailbox is excluded. Reply to the account's own latest sent
message is unsupported. A reply starts with empty Cc/body and one `Re:` prefix;
there is no reply-all, Bcc, signature, or automatic quoted text. Legacy cache
rows can use a readonly metadata-only Gmail fetch when online; cached metadata
hits are network-free. If that metadata is unavailable offline, reply preparation
is unavailable, while new-message and existing-draft editing remain local.

Native window Close and normal OS quit pause behind an in-memory
`app_close_requested` request. The UI flushes the current buffer, then completes
only that request after a durable receipt; failure/conflict cancels the request
and leaves the window and buffer open. Requests coalesce, stale IDs are rejected,
and completion without a pending native request cannot close the app. Browser
preview only models this protocol in memory and is never durable. Force quit,
crash, or power loss before a save ACK is not guaranteed to preserve the latest
keystrokes.

### Safe bulk selection and processing (UX-05)

Conversations can be selected in the Inbox/Done list with `X`, `Shift+J/K`,
Cmd/Ctrl-click, Shift-click ranges and per-row labelled checkboxes, bounded to
100 selected conversations per action (additive ranges; Select all loaded is
disabled with an explanation beyond the bound; selection clears on
context/account changes and survives reader visits with a visible bulk-scope
banner). Shared toolbar, palette and shortcut actions apply to the whole
selection when one exists (group path, even for one row); inline row actions
stay row-scoped, and Reply/open/navigation are never bulk.

A bulk action accepts one durable **operation group**: structure, duplicates,
bounds, request ID, active account and capability are validated before a single
SQLite transaction persists the group header, immutable per-member targets and
preimages, and per-member acceptance results. A gone/unactionable member becomes
a persisted typed rejection, not a fabricated failed provider operation;
all-rejected valid requests get an idempotent receipt and consume no Undo slot.
Same-request replays (including after restart) return the original receipt;
changed payloads are `request_id_conflict`. Archive/unarchive groups work in
fixture and Gmail mode; read/unread groups are Gmail-only, like the single
setters.

`Z` within the 10-second Rust-clock window undoes the latest top-level action,
whether a single or a group. A group Undo makes one durable attempt: queued
members are cancelled, applying/confirmed members are compensated from the
original preimages, and ineligible members (failed, unknown outcome, unknown
prior, already undone, acceptance-rejected) are explicitly skipped with reasons.
Partial results are worded honestly: the dock line stays short ("Restored 1 · 1
skipped — failed"; skips are named only when there are some) while its title and
accessible description keep the exact ledger ("Undo accepted for 1 of 2; 1
skipped (1 failed); …"), and per-member failures stay recoverable in Activity regardless of
current list rows. A rejected IPC acceptance is never treated as "nothing
happened": the UI keeps the original request ID and recovers via
`get_operation_group` / replay of the exact original request.

Browser-preview group behavior is modelled by the labelled in-memory fake, which
continues to disclose that it is non-durable; it makes no provider or storage
calls.

## UX-10 A — Read-only cached Trash (partial UX-10)

Gmail mode exposes **Go to cached Trash (read only)** in Commands and Destinations.
This lists known locally cached TRASH conversations, including operation-retained
snapshots; it does not discover Gmail Trash or claim mailbox-complete coverage.
Refresh is explicit, pagination is bounded, and Back preserves the loaded local
browsing state. Trash-origin readers omit mailbox actions and Reply. Opening
never marks read. The native fixture profile rejects this Gmail-only query;
browser-preview fixtures can simulate it in memory.

Observed per-message TRASH/SPAM facts now exclude those conversations from Inbox
and Done. Old profiles migrate with unknown (nullable) triage facts; unknown is
not asserted to be outside Trash/Spam. No mutation permission or provider write
was added. Existing archive/read durable intent, groups, Undo, Activity, local
drafts and close protections remain in place.

See [UX-10 bounded contracts and acceptance](ux-10-bounded-triage.md). Trash/recover
writes and Undo await a recovery-effects decision and a new durable dimension;
mute/spam writes, Important/Other, rules, Block and Unsubscribe are not enabled.
There is no permanent-delete/empty-Trash, arbitrary URL opener or send command.
Synthetic checks do not establish native WKWebView or remote Gmail convergence.
## UX-12 attachment capability and validation

See [UX-12 contract and evidence](ux-12-safe-attachments.md). The reader's Files
and links button (native Cmd+O) offers up to 32 cached descriptors and 32 literal
HTTP(S) links. No automatic read, file opening or URL dispatch occurs. Gmail
uses its existing readonly grant; only explicit Save issues attachment-endpoint
reads and decodes file bytes in Rust. Inline body-only parts without a fetchable
attachment ID are omitted; existing bounded full-thread reads can contain inline
payload fields, which are not decoded as attachments.
Missing/legacy descriptors need a sync; retained snapshots do not acquire new
provider authority. No attachment uploads, provider drafts or sending.

Saves create a unique file directly in OS Downloads with a `.download` suffix;
the frontend cannot supply a destination. Files never execute and must be
inspected/renamed outside the app. Cancel/dismiss discards an unfinished
transfer (a blocked HTTP call can take its existing 30-second timeout to return);
a completed save or process crash may leave an inert file. A lost save response
may leave a completed download; retries can create another unique file. Browser
preview only models a memory-only save and external handoff, not filesystem or
provider effects. External HTTP(S) dispatch currently targets macOS only.

PDF preview is **not implemented**: the restricted macOS platform sandbox and
compatibility spike has not passed. No PDF/HTML/Office document enters a webview,
trusted DOM or third-party viewer. Native build/bridge tests do not satisfy
WKWebView key handling, VoiceOver, Downloads permissions, OS browser dispatch,
or the PDF security spike. Disposable provider validation remains separately
operator-gated, not authorized by implementation work.

## Desktop-local reminder increment (UX-11)

See [the local reminder contract](ux-11-local-reminders.md) and
ADR 0001's reminder boundary. H / Remind me supports one Inbox conversation,
local time presets and free-text dates (or unscheduled Someday),
default If no reply / Regardless, and
Reminders pending/returned/history destinations (also G then H and palette).
Cancel/recover and reschedule are revisioned, durable commands. Pending stages
are not provider confirmation; returned membership requires confirmed return.
The existing fixture worker executes while running and reconciles overdue work
on launch. No execution while fully quit, cross-device state or calendar.

Gmail commands use local `gmail.db` reminders, immutable baseline IDs, a pinned
reader snapshot, account-scoped request receipts, and revision checks. They do
not enqueue Gmail archive or unarchive operations. Pending Inbox hiding ends
when a new message ID is observed. Regardless deadlines resolve locally. A
no-reply deadline needs a connected, complete fresh thread read. Offline,
incomplete, and failed reads stay pending. A provider reply can arrive after the
observed checkpoint and before commit; the decision is local and is not an
atomic provider absence guarantee. The browser fake supports memory-only reminder transport for UI tests and
development. Its due transitions reconcile on synthetic reads; they do not
establish native persistence or worker execution.
No credentials or real provider were used for this increment.

## Native prerequisites and platform limits

For a Debian/Ubuntu Linux VM, run the explicit setup task once:

```sh
mise run setup:linux
```

It runs `apt-get update`, then installs the compiler tools, `pkg-config`,
GTK/WebKitGTK development libraries, `librsvg2-dev`, and `dbus-daemon`. WebKitGTK
pulls in its Soup and JavaScriptCore dependencies. It also installs `xvfb`,
`xauth`, `xdotool`, `openbox`, `x11-utils`, and `scrot` for native window capture.
It uses `sudo` unless run as root. Re-running it keeps installed packages and
installs any missing ones; apt may update the listed packages.

The task rejects non-Linux hosts and hosts without `apt-get` before any package
operation. Other Linux distributions need equivalent packages installed manually.
It does not install mise runtimes or frontend dependencies. No build, check, or
macOS task depends on it. Do not run OS setup as part of an integration check.
macOS still uses Xcode command line tools and WKWebView, with the existing local
signing setup above.

### Native screenshots on a headless Linux VM

Use synthetic fixture mode and an isolated temporary data directory. Start the
app in a virtual X11 desktop from the repository root:

```sh
export EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/email-os-capture.XXXXXX)"
echo "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR"  # use this path in the second terminal
xvfb-run -a --server-args='-screen 0 1280x900x24 -nolisten tcp' sh -c '
  printf "%s\n" "$DISPLAY" > "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/display"
  printf "%s\n" "$XAUTHORITY" > "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/xauthority"
  openbox &
  export GDK_BACKEND=x11 EMAIL_OS_MODE=fixture
  export XDG_DATA_HOME="$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/data"
  exec dbus-run-session -- mise run dev:native
'
```

Wait for the native window to load. In a second terminal, set the printed path:

```sh
export EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/email-os-capture.XXXXXX  # replace with printed path
export DISPLAY="$(cat "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/display")"
export XAUTHORITY="$(cat "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/xauthority")"
xdotool windowactivate --sync "$(xdotool search --onlyvisible --class email-os | head -1)"
scrot -u -b "$EMAIL_OS_CAPTURE_DIR/native-inbox.png"
```

Use `xdotool` mouse/keyboard actions to open a conversation or Commands, then
capture another PNG. Stop the first terminal with Ctrl+C when finished. The
temporary directory retains the screenshots and isolated fixture data.
The default native task starts Vite on port 5173; free that port before launch.
For browser captures, run `mise run dev:web` and open its URL in the browser;
browser preview uses separate in-memory fixtures.

Linux native screenshots exercise WebKitGTK and the Rust fixture backend.
They do not validate macOS WKWebView/IME, Keychain prompts, system browser
launch, loopback OAuth interaction, or Google TLS behavior. Keep those Mac gates
separate. No sandbox or app security setting needs to be disabled for capture.

## Fixture data

Fixture mode uses only synthetic `fixture-account`, `conv-01`…`conv-18` rows,
seeded once; it never resets provider facts or operation history. Gmail mode has a
separate SQLite schema/profile and bounded cache. Neither mode logs subjects,
addresses, bodies, OAuth codes, or credentials. Gmail history catch-up does not
import arbitrary newly observed archived-thread bodies; the disclosed cache is
limited to up to 100 discovered conversations and may omit inbox threads outside
the bounded view.

<script setup lang="ts">
/**
 * Gmail mailbox shell: compact browsing shell (UX-01), plain-text reader,
 * operation recovery, and explicit account/action capability gates.
 *
 * Account gate: the account status read decides fixture-vs-Gmail. While the status
 * is loading or failed, the UI renders no mailbox content at all — it never falls
 * back silently to fixture mode.
 *
 * Layout contract: a persistent narrow email rail, a 78px split header in the
 * list column (no status line), one central surface that is either the list or the
 * reader (never both), and contact context. Account/Activity/Drafts live in
 * explicit labelled utility disclosures instead of permanent competing columns;
 * the contact pane shows only exact known fields.
 *
 * Keyboard contract (window-level, one handler):
 * - j / ArrowDown, k / ArrowUp: move conversation focus in the list (row focus
 *   follows). Inside the reader only j/k switch conversations; ArrowUp/Down
 *   keep native scrolling there.
 * - Enter: open the focused conversation. Escape: close the active utility or
 *   contact disclosure first, then the reader.
 * - e: archive the focused (or reader-open) conversation when actions are enabled.
 * - Shift+E: restore to Inbox; G then E (within 1000ms): cached Done.
 * - Left from list navigation: destination navigator; pointer Commands opens palette.
 * - Cmd+K opens the palette in native mode only (browser reservations stay native).
 * - c: compose a new local draft in the inline compose card in the central pane (works from list and reader).
 * - Shift+U: explicitly mark the focused/open conversation unread.
 * - z: undo the last accepted conversation action (single level, 10 s window;
 *   the backend's eligibility decision is authoritative). Cmd/Ctrl+Z is left
 *   to native text editing.
 * - Ignored with Ctrl/Meta/Alt held, during IME composition, inside text fields, and
 *   Enter/e are ignored when a button owns the key (it activates itself).
 * - While a visible draft editor exists, every mailbox shortcut is suppressed;
 *   a suspended editor behind another disclosure must not own keys. While a
 *   utility/contact disclosure is open, Escape closes it and mailbox shortcuts
 *   underneath are suppressed. Draft text has no submit/send path and is
 *   rendered only as ordinary text.
 */
import { computed, nextTick, onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref, watch } from 'vue';
import CachedTrashPanel from './components/CachedTrashPanel.vue';
import { emptyCachedTrash } from './lib/cached-trash';
import ActionOverlay from './components/ActionOverlay.vue';
import RemindersPanel from './components/RemindersPanel.vue';
import { formatReminderDateTime } from './lib/reminder-timezone';
import ReminderSettings from './components/ReminderSettings.vue';
import ActionNotice, { type GroupNoticeView } from './components/ActionNotice.vue';
import SelectionBar from './components/SelectionBar.vue';
import HeaderGlyph from './components/HeaderGlyph.vue';
import PaneGlyph from './components/PaneGlyph.vue';
import { browsingActions, actionLabel, type BrowsingActionId } from './lib/browsing-actions';
import { groupRowsBySender, isSingleFromQuery, senderGroupKey, validateSearch } from './lib/search';
import InboxList from './components/InboxList.vue';
import SplitEditor from './components/SplitEditor.vue';
import { splitBadge } from './lib/saved-split';
import type { SavedSplit } from './lib/ipc/client';
import ReaderView from './components/ReaderView.vue';
import AttachmentChooser from './components/AttachmentChooser.vue';
import ActivityPanel from './components/ActivityPanel.vue';
import AccountPanel from './components/AccountPanel.vue';
import DraftsPanel from './components/DraftsPanel.vue';
import ReplyComposer from './components/ReplyComposer.vue';
import ComposeCard from './components/ComposeCard.vue';
import ProviderDestinations from './components/ProviderDestinations.vue';
import ContactPane from './components/ContactPane.vue';
import FullDate from './components/FullDate.vue';
import { BROWSER_PREVIEW_DISCLOSURE } from './lib/ipc/browser-fake';
import type { ClientMode } from './lib/ipc';
import type { ConversationRef, DraftRef, DraftSource, MailClient, Reminder } from './lib/ipc/client';
import { sameConversation, useMailbox, type BrowseContext, type ConversationSummaryLike, type DoneBoundary, type SearchVisit, type LastActionId } from './composables/useMailbox';
import { useDrafts } from './composables/useDrafts';

const props = withDefaults(defineProps<{
  client: MailClient;
  mode: ClientMode;
  /** Only the visible in-app workspace may own global keys or focus. */
  active?: boolean;
  switchAccountLabel?: string;
}>(), { active: true });
const emit = defineEmits<{ switchAccount: []; workspaceTitle: [title: string] }>();
const workspaceActive = computed(() => props.active !== false);

/** Contact context breakpoint (supervisor-approved strict value). */
const CONTACT_BREAKPOINT_PX = 1000;

type UtilityDrawer = 'account' | 'activity' | 'drafts' | 'destinations' | 'reminders' | 'reminder-settings' | 'trash';
const trashState = ref(emptyCachedTrash());
type ContactContext = 'focused' | 'open';
interface ContactInfo { displayName: string | null; mailbox: string }
/** Visible-row anchor for the reader round trip. */
interface ListAnchor { ref: ConversationRef; offsetTop: number; scrollTop: number }
/**
 * Reader origin, captured ONLY at the initial list-to-reader entry. J/K inside
 * the reader and Activity opens while the reader is already open never
 * recapture from an unmounted list.
 */
interface ReaderOrigin {
  surface: BrowseContext | 'activity' | 'reminders' | 'trash';
  /** Original entry focus reference; Back restores it (with fallbacks). */
  focusedRef: ConversationRef | null;
  /** Entry-time Inbox ordering, used to resolve a removed cursor. */
  ordering: ConversationRef[];
  anchor: ListAnchor | null;
}

const mailbox = useMailbox(props.client);
/**
 * P5b: rows in rendered order — sender-grouped when the search context's
 * submitted query is a single non-excluded from: (InboxList renders exactly
 * this order), backend order everywhere else. Keyboard navigation, reader
 * J/K and the Back/anchor orderings all read this one definition so focus
 * walks the visible rows and never jumps across a sender caption.
 */
const listRows = computed<ConversationSummaryLike[]>(() =>
  mailbox.context.value === 'search' && isSingleFromQuery(mailbox.searchQuery.value) !== null
    ? groupRowsBySender(mailbox.conversations.value, senderGroupKey)
    : mailbox.conversations.value);

const editingSplit = ref(false);
const splitEditor = ref<InstanceType<typeof SplitEditor> | null>(null);
const contextTitle = computed(() => mailbox.context.value === 'search' ? 'Search' : mailbox.context.value === 'starred' ? 'Cached Starred' : mailbox.context.value === 'done' ? 'Cached Done' : mailbox.context.value === 'saved' ? mailbox.savedSplit.value?.name ?? 'Saved split' : 'Inbox');
const savedTabVisible = computed(() => mailbox.savedSplit.value?.enabled && !mailbox.splitError.value && (!mailbox.savedSplit.value.hideWhenEmpty || mailbox.savedTotal.value !== 0));

# Superhuman-inspired browsing: incremental implementation plan

**Status:** Proposed roadmap, not an implementation contract or authorization to access real mail.

Source: [Superhuman Email Browsing UX Specification](../superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md).
Existing constraints: [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md),
[development guide](development.md), and implementation contracts for
[Slices 01](vertical-slice-01.md), [02](vertical-slice-02.md),
[03](vertical-slice-03.md), and [04](vertical-slice-04.md).

## Recommendation

Build the browsing experience around the existing mail foundation, not as a replacement backend or a screenshot-only frontend. Deliver a working user journey in each slice:

```text
User input → Vue interaction state → typed MailClient/Tauri boundary
           → Rust query/command → SQLite/provider where needed
           → authoritative result/change hint → visible state and recovery
```

Start with **focus → open → read → back** in the new layout. Then introduce discovery, reversible triage, bulk processing, a saved split, and historical search. Stop at that useful browsing milestone before expandi

Use `UX-01` onward below to avoid confusing this roadmap with the repository's existing numbered implementation slices. These are delivery increments, not separate architectural layers. A slice must not wait for a later 

## 1. What exists and what must change

Source inspection, not a new runtime certification:

| Area | Current implementation | Consequence for this plan |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | Vue 3/TypeScript, thin Tauri 2 shell, Rust `mail-core`, SQLite | Preserve the stack and narrow typed boundaries |
| Mail access | Explicit single-account Gmail profile; bounded discovery of up to 100 conversations; plain-text cache; sync and freshness reporting | Cached rows are not the entire mailbox; browsing/search/counts need ex
| Actions | Durable archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread; immutable message targets, idempotency, reconciliation, Activity | Reuse execution machinery; Undo, groups, stars, labels, trash, etc. are new work |
| Drafts | Local-only composer, revisioned saves, safe reply preparation, native close/quit protocol | Rehouse rather than rewrite; preserve dirty-buffer and close protections |
| Layout | `App.vue` mounts list, reader, Activity, account and drafts panels; `style.css` has a multi-column utility layout | New list/reader modes and contact pane are a real layout change, not merely new colors |
| Focus | `useMailbox.ts` exposes `selectedIndex`, preserving identity during refresh; `InboxList.vue` treats focus as selection | Introduce explicit ID-based conversation focus, separate from future bulk selection |
| Reader | All plain-text messages expanded; no separate message focus | Add message focus/expansion without changing safe rendering or reply-source rules |
| Discovery | Inbox-only `listConversations()`; no search, split definitions, folder/label catalog, palette, or contact pane | Add bounded queries as the relevant slice needs them |
| Tests | Rust synthetic provider/storage tests; Vitest component/transport tests; in-memory browser fake | No existing real-browser E2E runner; fake IPC tests do not validate the native bridge |

1:# Superhuman-inspired browsing: incremental implementation plan
11:## Recommendation
25:## 1. What exists and what must change
52:## 2. Scope and fidelity decisions
62:## 3. Minimal shared design, introduced incrementally
64:### Separate mail state from browsing state
79:### One action catalog, not a generic executor
85:### Extend query contracts when contexts arrive
96:## 4. Delivery sequence
98:### UX-01 — A compact inbox that can actually be browsed
112:### UX-02 — Read a multi-message conversation without losing your place
126:### UX-03 — Discover actions and navigate to recoverable mail
140:### UX-04 — Process one conversation with trustworthy Undo
154:### UX-05 — Select and process several conversations safely
170:### UX-06 — One real saved split, not a classification engine
184:### UX-07 — Find older mail and return without losing the query
200:### UX-08 — Star a conversation and find it in Starred
211:### UX-09 — Browse labels/folders, then Label versus Move
226:### UX-10 — Broader triage, one explicit scope at a time
245:### UX-11 — Manual reminders with correct pending and returned states
263:### UX-12 — Safely inspect an attachment and return to the message
281:### UX-13 — Independent workspaces/accounts, then genuine native tabs
300:## 5. Validation is part of every slice
302:### Three evidence levels — do not conflate them
310:### A slice's completion record
323:### Cross-cutting quality checks, starting with UX-01
332:## 6. Traceability and release checkpoints
72:- UX-03: context/history and a topmost overlay; initially only inbox and cached Done.
128:**Journey:** Cmd+K → “go to Done” → open a cached archived conversation → Back to the exact prior inbox context.
130:- Introduce the shared action catalog and context-aware keyboard dispatcher. Start with implemented actions only: open/back, Done/Not Done, explicit read controls, account/Activity/drafts destinations, and Inbox/cached Done.
132:- Left opens a small destination navigator; support `G`, then `E` with a documented proposed timeout. Inbox and cached Done reuse rows/reader and a context history stack.
133:- Add a Rust read query for known locally archived/recovery conversations, including retained snapshots. Label this coverage honestly: it is not provider-complete Done/All Mail. Do not define Done as every thread lacking INBOX; future Sent/Spam/Trash membership must stay distinct.
136:**E2E checkpoint:** Archive a fixture thread, navigate to cached Done through palette and pointer, open it and return. Deny capabilities, delay destination responses and type `e/s/h` in the palette: no wrong-thread mutation. Preserve local drafts and normal-close protection after moving their entry points.
142:**Journey:** E marks Done → row/count/focus update → Z within 10 seconds restores the exact prior target state; explicit read/unread has the same recovery discipline.
147:- Initially support the latest eligible action only. Mixed read facts require restoring each prior value; unknown prior facts are not exactly undoable. Expiry and same-target newer actions are checked in Rust. Uncertain dispatched outcomes remain explicitly uncertain/reconciled, not falsely reported as undone.
213:Increment A contract and evidence: [bounded read-only provider destinations](ux-09-provider-destinations.md). Label/Move remains a separate unimplemented increment.
215:**Journey:** Left → label → open → L applies a tag without archiving → V moves by applying the destination and Done → recover.
