thread.title: Email OS P2: frontend test consolidation

items.text: I’ll read the repo guidance, record the test baseline, and check PR #34’s touched files first. Then I’ll delegate separable changes to GPT-6-Luna, review and validate them here, and open the two PRs without merging.

I’m applying the repository’s implement skill, with your explicit GPT-6-Luna delegation requirement. PR #34 touches 14 test/helper files, including drafts and discovery; I’ll keep those paths in place during Ticket 7 and list them as deferred.

The discovery race is in the test’s timing: it delays navigation by 50 ms, opens the palette, and assumes navigation is still pending. Under load, that delay can finish before the assertion. I’ll replace it with an explicitly controlled pending read. The baseline suite is running with one worker to limit VM load.

The first baseline run overlapped the helper edits, so I discarded it and restarted against a clean snapshot of the current commit. A second Luna agent is planning the timing changes; it will wait for the helper agent to release drafts and discovery before editing them.

The shared mount helper now has the requested client/mode API and centralized cleanup. The timing agent has taken over drafts and discovery to split the draft scenarios by concern and make their waits deterministic. The clean baseline is taking longer than expected on the shared VM; I’m checking that before relying on its results.

The clean baseline is progressing through the suite. The current test-title inventory matches it, with no static test cases removed or merged. During review I caught an accidental duplication from the helper migration script; both agents are correcting it before validation.

The clean baseline passed: **73 test files, 1,193 tests, zero failures and zero skips**. Four rendered suites are excluded from the default run and will be validated separately. The count-preservation checks now have a verified baseline.

The helper migration preserves event flags, IME `keyCode`, dispatch targets, mount attachment, and queue ordering explicitly. Draft timing changes are using a bounded virtual-time helper. I’ll validate Ticket 6 in isolation before committing it, so the two tickets remain separately reviewable even though their edits are progressing in parallel.

The timing changes are ready for focused validation. Draft reply preparation, account transitions, and close protocol tests are now split out, with their original test titles preserved. Discovery’s slow-navigation test holds the response behind an explicit deferred, so CPU load cannot release it early.

Focused validation found a test-split error: one account-transition case still referenced the old suite-local `wrapper`. It failed again when run alone, so this was a refactor bug, not a flake. I’ve corrected it and am rerunning the affected suites.

Focused timing validation passes: **86 tests across six files**. The draft and discovery clock now fixes `Date` and controls UI timeouts and intervals, removing wall-clock dependence from those tests.

The layout plan also found a fixture loaded by Rust through an exact path. I’ll keep that fixture in place to respect the Rust scope boundary.

Ticket 6 passes in isolation: **73 files, 1,193 tests, zero failures and zero skips**, matching the baseline. Typechecking also passes, and the test-title and assertion inventories are unchanged.

I’ll commit Ticket 6 now, then run Ticket 8’s three consecutive full-suite stress passes with two CPU hogs running.

The first stress run is progressing with both CPU hogs active. The reviewed layout plan keeps all PR #34 test paths in place and retains separate scenarios when merging small files.

I also rejected a proposed merge of the real-parser picker test into a suite that mocks the parser. It will join a suite using the real parser instead.
Stress run 1 passed: **76 files, 1,193 tests, zero failures or skips**, in **250.20 seconds**. Both CPU hogs stayed active. Run 2 is underway; I’m keeping the source unchanged through all three runs.

Stress run 2 passed: **76 files, 1,193 tests, zero failures or skips**, in **192.58 seconds**. Run 3 is underway.

The count plan is unchanged: 77 total files before maintenance, 80 after the draft split, then 73 after seven small-file merges. All 1,193 default cases and 34 rendered cases will remain.

All three stress runs passed with **1,193 tests, zero failures and zero skips** each. They took **250.20 s, 192.58 s, and 191.86 s** with two CPU hogs active; both hogs have now been stopped.

I’ll commit Ticket 8, open PR A, and start the layout-only commit for PR B.

[PR A is open](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/41), with one commit each for Tickets 6 and 8. Ticket 7 is now being applied on a branch stacked on PR A.

While the files move, I’ll run the rendered gate against an immutable snapshot of PR A to separate helper regressions from relocation issues.

The rendered run failed in shared setup before any test case ran: all four suites reported **`CDP timeout: Page.navigate`**, leaving 34 cases skipped. Chrome started, but navigation did not complete. I’ll rerun one case alone, then check whether the snapshot setup caused it.

The isolated suite reproduced the same setup failure. Vite responds to a direct HTTP request, but Chrome’s navigation has not reached it. I’m testing numeric loopback addressing in the temporary snapshot to narrow the cause. The repository’s rendered harness is unchanged.

The Chrome failure reproduces outside the repo: it renders a `data:` URL, but a standalone request to a synthetic HTTP server on loopback times out, including with proxy use disabled. I’ll leave the harness behavior unchanged, report that boundary precisely, and still run the required rendered command on the final layout.

Ticket 7 now has the planned **73 test files**. The static title inventory and stale-path checks are clean, including the two references in `DESIGN.md`.

Once the agent releases the files, I’ll run `check`, `build:web`, and the rendered command serially, with Rust using the shared target directory.

`mise run check` stopped on a Rust test outside this phase’s edit scope: **`undo_of_a_still_queued_operation_cancels_in_place_with_zero_provider_calls`**. I’ll rerun that test alone after the current serial gates finish and report whether it reproduces. The Rust sources remain untouched.

The Rust test passed alone, so I’ve recorded the first failure as an observed flake and will rerun the full check once. Its queued-state assertion raced with background processing: it returned `Compensating` where the test expected `Cancelled`.

The build also caught a duplicate Vitest import in the merged reminder-time suite. I removed it and will rerun the build.

The full check hit the same Rust race again: **314 passed, 1 failed, 0 ignored**. That is **2 failures in 2 full runs**, with **1 isolated pass**. I’ll report it without changing the Rust test or adding retries.

The web build now passes. I’ll run the frontend suite, contract check, lint and typecheck separately because the aggregate check stopped at the Rust failure.

The frontend run found two mock module paths missed during relocation. They caused five reminder-picker failures; the first case failed again alone. I’m correcting those paths and rerunning the picker suite, then the full frontend suite. The assertions stay unchanged.

The final frontend run passed: **69 files, 1,193 tests, zero failures and zero skips**. The picker suite also passed all nine tests after the path correction. Contract generation, core lint and typecheck pass.

The remaining validation limits are the unchanged Rust race and Chrome’s loopback navigation failure. I’m finishing the PR B commit and recording the evidence in both PRs.

[PR B is open](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/42), stacked on [PR A](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/41) and marked as depending on it. Both target `main`.

Both PRs now include the count-preservation evidence, stress results, deferred paths, and the Rust and Chrome validation limits. I’m checking the remote head SHAs and working-tree state before handing back.

Both PRs are open against `main`; B depends on A.

- [PR A #41](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/41): Ticket 6 shared helpers; Ticket 8 deterministic timing and draft-suite split. Head: `2644f4c115ce61a9b7cda41310e0146285daf3ed`
- [PR B #42](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/pull/42): Ticket 7 feature folders, seven small-file consolidations and path-reference updates. Head: `bb7b19ccd5855eecc612868a8a85731db27164ea`

| Checkpoint | Total test files | Default passed / failed / skipped |
|---|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 77 | 1,193 / 0 / 0 |
| Ticket 6 | 77 | 1,193 / 0 / 0 |
| Ticket 8 | 80 | 1,193 / 0 / 0 |
| Ticket 7 | 73 | 1,193 / 0 / 0 |

All 34 rendered cases remain. No scenarios were deleted.

Stress validation passed **three consecutive runs**, taking **250.20s, 192.58s and 191.86s**, with two CPU hogs active. Both hogs were stopped.

Web build, typecheck, contract generation and core lint pass. Two gates remain unsuccessful:

- **`mise run check`:** 314 Rust tests passed, 1 failed, 0 ignored. `undo_of_a_still_queued_operation_cancels_in_place_with_zero_provider_calls` failed **2/2 full runs** but passed **1/1 isolated run**. Rust sources remain unchanged.
- **Rendered:** all four suites were found, but four setup failures left **0 passed, 34 skipped**. Exact error: **`CDP timeout: Page.navigate`**. Standalone Chrome also timed out on synthetic loopback HTTP.

Deferred: PR #34’s 14 test/helper paths, plus `tests/fixtures/newest-sender-summaries.json`. The [handoff manifest](/tmp/email-os-p2-validation.json) lists every path and validation artifact.

Coordinator: address the two gates above, merge A before rebasing B, then run account-transit, draft recovery/close, and IME/palette/reader end-to-end checks. Working tree is clean.

You are one implementation thread in a coordinated maintenance programme for Email OS, following a code review. A coordinating thread (not you) sequences the phases, merges PRs and runs end-to-end validation between phases. This is implementation, not another review.

HOW TO WORK
- The user explicitly requires this top-level thread to run GPT-6.1-Sol and to implement through GPT-6-Luna subagents where the work can be split: use native spawn_agent with model gpt-6-luna (fork_turns: none where supported), give each a full scoped brief, the checkout path and non-overlapping files, then review and integrate their changes yourself. No replacement models. Do small or tightly coupled edits yourself rather than delegating for its own sake. The user's model choice overrides any model default in repository skills.
- Read the repository instructions, docs/current-architecture.md, docs/current-status.md and docs/development.md first.
- You are in an isolated worktree created from origin/main at 5df839d. Do not edit the root checkout /home/exedev/email-os or its local .codex/hooks.json change.

MACHINE LIMITS (these matter)
- 2 CPU cores, 7 GB RAM, about 8 GB free disk, shared with other threads.
- Export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target for every cargo/mise command. It is a shared build cache and the one path under the root checkout you may write; a private target dir per worktree costs about 4 GB and will fill the disk. Never hardcode a target dir in mise.toml or scripts. Cargo may wait on its lock; that is expected.
- Run at most one heavy command (cargo build/test, vitest) at a time in this thread, including across subagents.
- The worktree has no node_modules; run `mise run install:ui` before `mise run check`.

RULES FOR EVERY TICKET
- Behaviour-preserving. This phase owns Rust test code: crates/mail-core/tests/, the #[cfg(test)] modules under crates/mail-core/src/, the test helpers in src-tauri/src/main.rs, and dev-dependencies. No change to production behaviour. A test-only seam is acceptable if it is compiled out of release builds; if you believe you have found a real production race rather than a test race, stop and report it with evidence instead of patching it.
- No test is deleted or weakened without naming the test that replaces it; report test counts before and after (baseline: 315 mail-core tests, 11 or 12 email-os tests).
- Similar-looking scenarios often verify different guarantees (restart, lost ACK, stale response, account isolation). Consolidate fakes and helpers, not scenarios.
- Synthetic fixtures only: no real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- If a ticket turns out to be wrong about the code, or you hit a decision outside your scope, stop and report instead of guessing.

TICKET 4: shared Rust test support
- Four integration files each carry their own fake implementation of the GmailReadProvider trait plus 240 to 720 lines of setup before the first test: crates/mail-core/tests/gmail_operations.rs, gmail_cache_sync.rs, undo.rs, provider_destinations.rs. Two more fakes live in source test modules (crates/mail-core/src/gmail/reply_context_sync_tests.rs and the test module at the bottom of crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs). Helpers are copied between files: temp_profile (5 copies), until, open_core and TIMEOUT (4 each), FakeState (3), ApplyPlan (2). tests/support/stars.rs is pulled in with #[path].
- Build one scripted fake provider and one set of helpers (until/wait helpers, open_core, thread/message/profile builders) that all of these use. Choose the mechanism deliberately and say why: a tests/support module for the integration files, or a `test-support` cargo feature exposing a testing module that both integration and in-source tests use (dev-dependency on the crate itself with that feature). Prefer the option that leaves exactly one fake implementation; if the in-source tests genuinely need crate-private access the shared fake cannot give, keep those minimal and explain.
- Replace every ad-hoc temp directory with tempfile::TempDir (add the dev-dependency), including the helpers in src-tauri/src/main.rs tests and the #[cfg(test)] modules. Today tests leak profile directories into /tmp on every run (about 2,800 had accumulated).
- Done when: there is one fake GmailReadProvider implementation (or a justified, documented minimum), no duplicated helper remains, test counts are unchanged, and a full `cargo test -p mail-core` followed by `cargo test -p email-os` leaves no new entries in /tmp (count before and after).

TICKET 5: deterministic worker control; fix the flaky undo suite (after Ticket 4)
- crates/mail-core/tests/undo.rs is flaky. The coordinator saw it fail 5 of 15 runs; another thread saw it fail 2 of 2 full `mise run check` runs. Tests that have failed, with the observed cause:
  - undo_of_a_still_queued_operation_cancels_in_place_with_zero_provider_calls: it waits for status Queued, which is already true at acceptance, so the worker can claim the operation before the undo lands and the receipt is Compensating instead of Cancelled.
  - undoable_until_survives_a_restart_within_the_window_and_expires_after_it: same shape after the restart; the requeued operation can be reclaimed before the undo.
  - compensation_targets_exclude_messages_that_arrived_after_the_original: core.request_sync() returned Busy because a pass was still running.
  - cached_done_excludes_cancelled_and_undone_archives_but_keeps_failed_compensation: an until(...) poll for Confirmed ran out.
- The suites poll real worker threads against the wall clock. Give the shared fake provider explicit gates (hold an operation or a sync pass at a named stage until the test releases it; wait for idle before requesting a sync) and use them wherever a test currently assumes the worker has not yet moved. Keep the real worker and real store in the loop; do not replace them with mocks.
- Audit the other suites for the same pattern while you are there (gmail_operations.rs, gmail_cache_sync.rs, reminders.rs, integration.rs, and the sleep-based reminder/backoff tests in the sync.rs test module) and fix what you find; list anything you leave.
- Done when: `cargo test -p mail-core --test undo` passes 50 consecutive runs and the full `cargo test -p mail-core` passes 10 consecutive runs, both while two CPU hogs run in the background (for example two `yes > /dev/null` processes, killed afterwards). Report the loop output, not just the claim.

VALIDATION BEFORE YOU HAND BACK
- mise run check; mise run test:native; mise run build:web. Report exact pass/fail/skip counts.
- cargo fmt and clippy -D warnings for both crates (`cargo clippy --locked -p mail-core -p email-os --all-targets -- -D warnings`).

DELIVERY
- One commit per ticket (split further if it helps review). Push the branch and open ONE pull request against main (gh needs `-R BbrSofiane/email-os` because the git remote is a proxy URL). Do not merge.
- Final message: PR URL, head SHA, what changed per ticket, the chosen sharing mechanism and why, before/after test counts, the stress-loop evidence, anything left and why, and anything the coordinator should check end to end.

input.message:
You are one implementation thread in a coordinated maintenance programme for Email OS, following a code review. A coordinating thread (not you) sequences the phases, merges PRs and runs end-to-end validation between phases. This is implementation, not another review.

HOW TO WORK
- The user explicitly requires this top-level thread to run GPT-6.1-Sol and to implement through GPT-6-Luna subagents where the work can be split: use native spawn_agent with model gpt-6-luna (fork_turns: none where supported), give each a full scoped brief, the checkout path and non-overlapping files, then review and integrate their changes yourself. No replacement models. Do small or tightly coupled edits yourself rather than delegating for its own sake. The user's model choice overrides any model default in repository skills.
- Read the repository instructions, docs/current-architecture.md, docs/current-status.md and docs/development.md first.
- You are in an isolated worktree created from origin/main at 5df839d. Do not edit the root checkout /home/exedev/email-os or its local .codex/hooks.json change.

MACHINE LIMITS (these matter)
- 2 CPU cores, 7 GB RAM, about 8 GB free disk, shared with other threads.
- Export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target for every cargo/mise command. It is a shared build cache and the one path under the root checkout you may write; a private target dir per worktree costs about 4 GB and will fill the disk. Never hardcode a target dir in mise.toml or scripts. Cargo may wait on its lock; that is expected.
- Run at most one heavy command (cargo build/test, vitest) at a time in this thread, including across subagents.
- The worktree has no node_modules; run `mise run install:ui` before `mise run check`.

RULES FOR EVERY TICKET
- Behaviour-preserving. This phase owns Rust test code: crates/mail-core/tests/, the #[cfg(test)] modules under crates/mail-core/src/, the test helpers in src-tauri/src/main.rs, and dev-dependencies. No change to production behaviour. A test-only seam is acceptable if it is compiled out of release builds; if you believe you have found a real production race rather than a test race, stop and report it with evidence instead of patching it.
- No test is deleted or weakened without naming the test that replaces it; report test counts before and after (baseline: 315 mail-core tests, 11 or 12 email-os tests).
- Similar-looking scenarios often verify different guarantees (restart, lost ACK, stale response, account isolation). Consolidate fakes and helpers, not scenarios.
- Synthetic fixtures only: no real accounts, credentials or Google network.
- If a ticket turns out to be wrong about the code, or you hit a decision outside your scope, stop and report instead of guessing.

TICKET 4: shared Rust test support
- Four integration files each carry their own fake implementation of the GmailReadProvider trait plus 240 to 720 lines of setup before the first test: crates/mail-core/tests/gmail_operations.rs, gmail_cache_sync.rs, undo.rs, provider_destinations.rs. Two more fakes live in source test modules (crates/mail-core/src/gmail/reply_context_sync_tests.rs and the test module at the bottom of crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs). Helpers are copied between files: temp_profile (5 copies), until, open_core and TIMEOUT (4 each), FakeState (3), ApplyPlan (2). tests/support/stars.rs is pulled in with #[path].
- Build one scripted fake provider and one set of helpers (until/wait helpers, open_core, thread/message/profile builders) that all of these use. Choose the mechanism deliberately and say why: a tests/support module for the integration files, or a `test-support` cargo feature exposing a testing module that both integration and in-source tests use (dev-dependency on the crate itself with that feature). Prefer the option that leaves exactly one fake implementation; if the in-source tests genuinely need crate-private access the shared fake cannot give, keep those minimal and explain.
- Replace every ad-hoc temp directory with tempfile::TempDir (add the dev-dependency), including the helpers in src-tauri/src/main.rs tests and the #[cfg(test)] modules. Today tests leak profile directories into /tmp on every run (about 2,800 had accumulated).
- Done when: there is one fake GmailReadProvider implementation (or a justified, documented minimum), no duplicated helper remains, test counts are unchanged, and a full `cargo test -p mail-core` followed by `cargo test -p email-os` leaves no new entries in /tmp (count before and after).

TICKET 5: deterministic worker control; fix the flaky undo suite (after Ticket 4)
- crates/mail-core/tests/undo.rs is flaky. The coordinator saw it fail 5 of 15 runs; another thread saw it fail 2 of 2 full `mise run check` runs. Tests that have failed, with the observed cause:
  - undo_of_a_still_queued_operation_cancels_in_place_with_zero_provider_calls: it waits for status Queued, which is already true at acceptance, so the worker can claim the operation before the undo lands and the receipt is Compensating instead of Cancelled.
  - undoable_until_survives_a_restart_within_the_window_and_expires_after_it: same shape after the restart; the requeued operation can be reclaimed before the undo.
  - compensation_targets_exclude_messages_that_arrived_after_the_original: core.request_sync() returned Busy because a pass was still running.
  - cached_done_excludes_cancelled_and_undone_archives_but_keeps_failed_compensation: an until(...) poll for Confirmed ran out.
- The suites poll real worker threads against the wall clock. Give the shared fake provider explicit gates (hold an operation or a sync pass at a named stage until the test releases it; wait for idle before requesting a sync) and use them wherever a test currently assumes the worker has not yet moved. Keep the real worker and real store in the loop; do not replace them with mocks.
- Audit the other suites for the same pattern while you are there (gmail_operations.rs, gmail_cache_sync.rs, reminders.rs, integration.rs, and the sleep-based reminder/backoff tests in the sync.rs test module) and fix what you find; list anything you leave.
- Done when: `cargo test -p mail-core --test undo` passes 50 consecutive runs and the full `cargo test -p mail-core` passes 10 consecutive runs, both while two CPU hogs run in the background (for example two `yes > /dev/null` processes, killed afterwards). Report the loop output, not just the claim.

VALIDATION BEFORE YOU HAND BACK
- mise run check; mise run test:native; mise run build:web. Report exact pass/fail/skip counts.
- cargo fmt and clippy -D warnings for both crates (`cargo clippy --locked -p mail-core -p email-os --all-targets -- -D warnings`).

DELIVERY
- One commit per ticket (split further if it helps review). Push the branch and open ONE pull request against main (gh needs `-R BbrSofiane/email-os` because the git remote is a proxy URL). Do not merge.
- Final message: PR URL, head SHA, what changed per ticket, the chosen sharing mechanism and why, before/after test counts, the stress-loop evidence, anything left and why, and anything the coordinator should check end to end.

content.thinking:
I'm seeing that these five failures look like stale test expectations rather than real bugs: the rendered tests fell behind product changes, like a reminder row action added in #33 and a palette reorder. They already fail on main, since that suite never runs by default and hangs on DBus in this VM. I'm noting a harness ticket to neutralize DBus through the environment so it can run here.

I'm planning a follow-up ticket to fix the five stale rendered tests, updating their expectations only after confirming each is outdated rather than a real product bug, and getting the suite green. Since it's the closest thing to automated end-to-end UI validation, I'm considering wiring it into check:all or CI. I'm leaning toward stacking it as a new PR on top of #42, since the rendered test files are the ones that branch moves.

I'm weighing whether to check #41 and #42 myself before merging, since the thread's stress run looks credible but I shouldn't switch branches in the root checkout, which has the user's uncommitted hooks change. A separate git worktree in scratch space would let me run the frontend suite on the #42 head, which includes #41, without touching that state. I'm settling on a merge order of #40 once CI is green, then #41, then #42, then the rendered-fix PR.

I'm noting that CI only arrives with #40, so once #40 merges I'd rebase #41 and #42 onto main to get CI runs on them. Then I'll write the follow-up message to P2, covering the root cause and evidence, the fix approach, the baseline failure list with messages, and instructions.

input.message:
Coordinator follow-up. PRs #41 and #42 look good; thank you for the count evidence. Two things before they merge, both about the rendered suite, which is our only automated end-to-end check of the UI.

1. ROOT CAUSE OF `CDP timeout: Page.navigate` (I reproduced and fixed it locally; it is not a loopback or proxy problem)
On this VM, Chrome's first navigation blocks for about 24 s on DBus calls that never get an answer (stderr shows `Failed to call method: org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.GetDevices` and UPower; 25 s is the DBus default timeout). The harness gives each CDP command 20 s, so Page.navigate always times out. Evidence from a script replicating tests/rendered/chromium.ts step by step: with the default environment, frameStartedNavigating at 3.2 s and Page.navigate returning at 25.7 s; with DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and DBUS_SYSTEM_BUS_ADDRESS pointed at nonexistent sockets, navigate returns in 0.6 s and the app is ready at 5 s.
Fix it in the harness: spawn Chrome with an env that neutralises both DBus addresses (for example `unix:path=/nonexistent`), with a comment saying why. Headless test Chrome needs no DBus. Do not raise the 20 s timeout instead.

2. FIVE RENDERED TESTS FAIL ON MAIN ONCE THE HARNESS RUNS (baseline on 5df839d with the DBus workaround: 29 passed, 5 failed, 34 total, 62 s)
These have apparently never run in this VM, so they have drifted from the product:
- discovery.rendered: "types in the focused palette with zero mutations, highlights, contains Tab and restores focus" at about line 454: after ArrowDown the selected option is "Open conversationEnter", test expects "Mark done" (the palette order changed, e.g. Compose/Reply were added).
- inbox-list.rendered-layout: both tests (about lines 260 and 335): row actions are now mark-read, mark-unread, remind, archive; tests expect no `row-remind-conv-01` (reminders landed in #33).
- reader.rendered: "UX-12 download chooser restores exact reader state without rendering attachments or loading resources" at about line 182: a dialog text expectation is false.
- reader.rendered: "keeps a directly focused participant override through the active-message handoff from a different active message" at about line 608: a `[data-test="messag..."]` presence expectation is false.
For EACH of the five, decide with evidence whether the test is stale (the product changed deliberately: cite the commit or contract doc) or the product regressed. Update stale tests to the current behaviour without weakening what they protect (for example, the row-actions test should now assert the remind control too and still check the layout). If you conclude any of them is a real product regression, do not touch src/: report it to me with the evidence and leave that test failing.

Delivery
- Put this in a new PR C stacked on PR B (#42), so A and B stay as reviewed: one commit for the harness fix, one for the stale tests. If the harness fix conflicts with nothing, that is all C needs.
- Done when `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome mise run test:rendered` passes on PR C's head with no wrapper script (34 of 34, or 34 minus any regressions you reported), twice in a row, and the default suite still shows 1,193 passing.
- Also add a line to docs/development.md next to the test:rendered instructions explaining the DBus note, and say in your report whether the rendered suite is now stable enough to add to `check:all` and CI (a sibling PR #40 adds .github/workflows/ci.yml; do not edit that file, just tell me what Chrome install step it would need).
- Other threads are running Rust builds on this 2-core machine. One heavy command at a time; the rendered suite starts four Vite servers and four Chromes, so do not run it alongside the full default suite.
Report PR URL, head SHA, the per-test verdicts and the two run results. Still do not merge.

#!/bin/bash
# Native end-to-end smoke for Email OS (fixture mode, WebKitGTK under Xvfb).
# usage: smoke-native.sh <checkout-dir> <run-dir> [seed-data-dir]
#   Builds the app from <checkout-dir>, runs the keyboard journey, closes normally,
#   relaunches, and checks SQLite state. With [seed-data-dir] it instead starts from a
#   copy of an existing profile (upgrade check) and only verifies that state survives.
# Coordinator tooling; lives in the session scratchpad, not in the repo.
set -u
CHECKOUT="$1"; RUN="$2"; SEED="${3:-}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target
mkdir -p "$RUN"; rm -rf "$RUN/data" "$RUN"/*.png
FAIL=0
ok()   { echo "  ok   $*"; }
bad()  { echo "  FAIL $*"; FAIL=1; }
check(){ local name="$1" got="$2" want="$3"; if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then ok "$name = $got"; else bad "$name: got [$got] want [$want]"; fi; }

echo "== build ($(git -C "$CHECKOUT" rev-parse --short HEAD) $(git -C "$CHECKOUT" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD))"
( cd "$CHECKOUT" && { [ -d node_modules ] || mise exec -- pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; } >"$RUN/install.log" 2>&1 \
  && mise exec -- pnpm build >"$RUN/web-build.log" 2>&1 \
  && mise exec -- cargo build --locked -p email-os --features custom-protocol >"$RUN/cargo-build.log" 2>&1 ) \
  || { echo "BUILD FAILED"; tail -15 "$RUN/web-build.log" "$RUN/cargo-build.log" 2>/dev/null; exit 2; }
cp "$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/email-os" "$RUN/email-os"

launch() {
  rm -f "$RUN/display" "$RUN/xauthority"
  setsid "$HERE/launch.sh" "$RUN" >"$RUN/xvfb.log" 2>&1 &
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do [ -s "$RUN/xauthority" ] && break; sleep 0.5; done
  export DISPLAY="$(cat "$RUN/display")" XAUTHORITY="$(cat "$RUN/xauthority")"
  WIN=""
  for i in $(seq 1 80); do WIN="$(xdotool search --onlyvisible --class email-os 2>/dev/null | head -1)"; [ -n "$WIN" ] && break; sleep 0.5; done
  [ -n "$WIN" ] || { bad "window never appeared"; return 1; }
  xdotool windowactivate --sync "$WIN"; xdotool windowfocus --sync "$WIN"; xdotool mousemove 640 30
  sleep 4
}
running(){ pgrep -f "$RUN/email-o[s]" >/dev/null; }
close_app() {
  xdotool key alt+F4
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do running || { ok "normal close exited the app"; return 0; }; sleep 0.5; done
  bad "app still running 15 s after normal close"; pkill -f "$RUN/email-o[s]"; sleep 1
}
k()    { xdotool key "$@"; sleep 0.8; }
shot() { scrot -o -a 90,57,1100,785 "$RUN/$1.png"; }
PROFILE="$RUN/data/dev.exedev.email-os.fixture/fixture-profile"
q()    { sqlite3 "$PROFILE/mail.db" "$1" 2>&1; }
qd()   { sqlite3 "$PROFILE/local-drafts/drafts.db" "$1" 2>&1; }
DRAFT='{"to":"smoke@example.test","cc":"","subject":"Smoke subject","bodyText":"Smoke body line more"}'

if [ -z "$SEED" ]; then
  echo "== phase 1: journey on a fresh profile"
  launch || exit 1
  shot 01-inbox
  k j; k Return; sleep 1; shot 02-reader
  k Escape
  k e; sleep 2; shot 03-archived
  k z; sleep 2; shot 04-undone
  k e; sleep 2
  k x; k shift+j; shot 05-selected
  k e; sleep 3; shot 06-group-archived
  k c; sleep 1
  xdotool type --delay 30 'smoke@example.test'; k Tab; k Tab
  xdotool type --delay 30 'Smoke subject'; k Tab
  xdotool type --delay 30 'Smoke body line'; sleep 1.5; shot 07-compose
  xdotool type --delay 30 ' more'; sleep 0.2
  close_app
else
  echo "== phase 1 skipped: seeding profile from $SEED"
  mkdir -p "$RUN/data"; cp -a "$SEED/." "$RUN/data/"
fi

echo "== state after first session"
check "operations"            "$(q 'select count(*) from operations')" 5
check "confirmed operations"  "$(q "select count(*) from operations where status='confirmed'")" 5
check "undo operations"       "$(q 'select count(*) from operations where undo_of is not null')" 1
check "operation groups"      "$(q 'select count(*) from operation_groups')" 1
check "group members w/ op"   "$(q 'select count(*) from operation_group_members where operation_id is not null')" 2
check "archived conversations" "$(q "select group_concat(conversation_id, ',') from (select conversation_id from operations where requested_archived=1 and undo_of is null group by conversation_id order by conversation_id)")" "conv-14,conv-16,conv-17"
check "drafts"                "$(qd 'select count(*) from drafts')" 1
check "draft content"         "$(qd 'select content_json from drafts')" "$DRAFT"
OPS_BEFORE="$(q 'select operation_id, status from operations order by seq')"

echo "== phase 2: relaunch on the same profile"
launch || exit 1
shot 08-relaunch-inbox
k j; k Return; sleep 1; shot 09-relaunch-reader; k Escape
close_app
check "operations unchanged by relaunch" "$(q 'select operation_id, status from operations order by seq')" "$OPS_BEFORE"
check "draft survives relaunch" "$(qd 'select content_json from drafts')" "$DRAFT"
grep -i -E 'panic|thread .* panicked' "$RUN/app.log" && bad "panic in app log" || ok "no panic in app log"

( cd "$RUN" && convert 0[1-9]-*.png -resize 50% -append sheet.png 2>/dev/null )
echo "== result: $([ $FAIL = 0 ] && echo PASS || echo FAIL)  (screens: $RUN/sheet.png)"
exit $FAIL

items.text:
Coordinator follow-up on PR #40. The diff looks good, but the CI run you added failed (run 42774204109, job "check"), so it cannot merge yet:

  [lint:core] error: 'cargo-fmt' is not installed for the toolchain '1.89.0-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'.

A fresh `mise install` gives a toolchain without rustfmt and clippy; this VM only works because they were added by hand at some point. Please:
1. Fix it at the source so any fresh machine works, not just CI: declare the components with the pinned toolchain in mise.toml (for example `rust = { version = "1.89.0", components = "rustfmt,clippy" }`) if mise supports that for this version; otherwise add an explicit rustup component step and document it in docs/development.md. Verify whichever you choose actually installs both.
2. Replace `curl https://mise.run | sh` in the workflow with a pinned install (the jdx/mise-action at a pinned version is fine).
3. Push, wait for the CI run on the PR, and iterate until it is green. If it fails on the known flaky crates/mail-core/tests/undo.rs tests, rerun the job once and report which test failed; do not add retries. Any other failure is yours to fix.
4. Another thread ("Email OS P1: Rust test foundations") is now running Rust builds. Keep CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target and one heavy command at a time; prefer letting CI do the full run rather than repeating check:all locally.

Report back with the green run URL and the new head SHA. Still do not merge.
I’ll check mise’s component support, fix the pinned toolchain setup, and pin the workflow installer. I’ll verify component installation locally, then let PR CI run the full suite.

The toolchain declaration now requests `rustfmt` and `clippy` with Rust 1.89.0’s minimal profile. I’m testing it with empty, isolated mise, Cargo and rustup homes, so the VM’s existing components cannot mask a failure. The workflow now uses a commit-pinned `jdx/mise-action` and mise 2026.11.3.

The fresh install succeeded: rustfmt 1.8.0 and clippy 0.1.89 are both installed and executable. I pushed `c6d13fd` to PR #40. I’ll monitor CI and address any failure, without repeating the full suite locally.

thread.title: Email OS P1: Rust test foundations

items.text: I’ll read the repository guidance and architecture docs, then split the test-support work into scoped Luna tasks. I’ll keep builds sequential and use the shared Cargo cache.

I’m applying the repository’s implement skill. The fake consolidation and worker controls are closely coupled, so I’ll give one Luna implementation agent ownership of both tickets, then review and validate the result here. A `test-support` feature looks promising for sharing one fake across integration and source tests; the agent will check that against the code first.

The worktree was clean, and the baseline core tests are running. I confirmed that `mise run check` normally runs several tasks in parallel; I’ll use `-j 1` to respect the machine limit. All Cargo builds will use the shared target directory.

The queued-undo tests need a control point before the worker claims an operation. A provider-call gate acts after the claim, so it cannot guarantee that Undo sees `Queued`. I’ve flagged that distinction for the implementation: use a test-only claim control for queued cancellation, while keeping provider gates for applying and sync scenarios.

The baseline run reproduced a timeout in `uncertain_failed_and_compensating_operations_are_not_undoable` while waiting for `Confirmed`. I’ll retain that failure log and use test discovery to establish the full baseline count, since Cargo stopped before running every suite. The temp-directory audit also found leaks beyond the six fake-provider files; those are included in Ticket 4’s scope.

The existing fakes cover different guarantees—auth changes, cancellation, destination admission and lost responses—so consolidation needs to preserve each scenario. The agent has started replacing profile paths with owned `TempDir` values. I’m also checking that the queued-undo fix preserves the zero-dispatch assertion for the cancelled operation.

I’ve split the independent TempDir cleanup into a second Luna task with separate files. The first agent owns the shared fake and worker-control changes; the second owns the remaining source-test and native-test directory cleanup. Builds remain sequential, and I’ll review both diffs together before validation.

The worker-control change will use a test-only paused-mutations constructor. Auth, sync and SQLite will still run normally, while queued-cancellation tests can hold mutation claims until after Undo. The flag and constructor will be excluded from default release builds.

TempDir conversion is still in progress across the integration and source tests. The claim-pause seam is drafted, but the shared provider is not yet complete. I’m keeping that consolidation as the priority before stress testing; there’s no Ticket 4 commit ready for review yet.

The first compile check found mechanical errors in the TempDir conversion, including two replacements in production path handling. I’ve sent those back to the owning agent for correction. I’ll review the affected diffs before testing again; the changes must stay within test code and the gated worker-control seam.

I checked the baseline totals: 315 core tests ran, with 314 passing and one undo timeout. The TempDir changes and shared helper feature now compile for the undo suite. The six provider implementations still need consolidation before Ticket 4 can be considered complete.

Frontend dependencies are installed for the final checks. I’m reviewing TempDir ownership, especially helpers that return a core or store: the directory guard must remain alive through use and restart so cleanup cannot happen early.

The harness fix gets Chrome through startup, and the baseline now reproduces the five reported failures. The evidence points to stale tests: the palette contract specifies keyboard selection rather than a fixed result order; reminders add a documented row action; the chooser’s short copy is documented in `DESIGN.md`; and the participant test clicks Details while its message is collapsed.

I’ll update those expectations and setup steps while retaining the layout, focus, state-restoration and zero-mutation checks.

The updated expectations exposed a product issue in the large-text Inbox case. At a 1,000px viewport and 30px root font, the row reports **671px scroll width against 661px client width**, violating the existing no-horizontal-overflow assertion.

The first Inbox case and both repaired reader cases pass. I’m rerunning the overflow case alone before reporting it as a regression; I’ll leave its geometry assertion and `src/` unchanged.

The overflow reproduces alone: **671px scroll width versus 661px client width**, after the resize/frame waits. UX-01 requires actions to move behind the disclosure when space runs out, with no horizontal overflow, so I’m classifying the large-text Inbox case as a product regression and keeping it failing.

I’ll now run the final PR C head twice with the exact rendered command. The expected result is **33 passed, 1 reported regression, 0 skipped** per run, followed by the default suite.

The default suite passed **1,193/1,193**. The web build caught one type declaration that also needs updating: this repo’s minimal Node shim allows only `stdio` in `spawn` options, so it rejects the new `env` field.

I’ll add the optional `env` type and fold it into the harness commit, keeping the requested two-commit structure. Then I’ll rerun the build and both rendered runs on the rewritten final head.

The final-head web build passes, including typechecking the corrected Node shim. PR C still has exactly two commits, and A/B are unchanged. The rewritten head’s two rendered runs are in progress; they should retain the reported overflow failure rather than skip or weaken it.

The rewritten head’s first rendered run finished in **85.04s**: **33 passed, only the known overflow failed, 0 skipped**. The second run is underway. No navigation failures or additional test failures appeared in the first run.

The second rewritten-head run also hit 5-second Vitest timeouts in two multi-workspace journeys, beyond the consistent overflow failure. Both workspace journeys passed alone, in **1.92s** and **1.41s**. Each timed out once across five full post-repair runs, exhausting Vitest’s 5-second whole-test budget under load.

input.message:
Coordinator: main moved again while you were syncing. The user's UI work merged as PRs #31 (drawer panels) and #32 (list contexts); main is now 078e177. Relative to 2f79235 that adds 16 test files and modifies 19 under tests/ (about 4,900 lines), and GitHub now reports #41 and #42 as CONFLICTING. New files include tests/context-row-list.component.test.ts, draft-previews.test.ts, drafts-list.component.test.ts, drafts.context.test.ts, drawer-panels.app.test.ts, list-context-header.test.ts, list-context-keys.test.ts, mailbox.local-contexts.test.ts, reminders.context.test.ts, reminders.helpers.ts, reminders.list.test.ts, subject-index.test.ts, use-drawer-rows.component.test.ts, useDrafts.discard-listed.test.ts, useMailbox.trash.test.ts, useReminders.test.ts.

Main will keep moving, so the goal now is to land this stack quickly and correctly:
1. Merge origin/main (078e177 or newer; fetch first) into A, then carry up into B and C. Resolve conflicts in favour of main's test intent: where main changed a test you had migrated, re-apply your helper migration to main's new version of that test, do not keep your older copy of its assertions.
2. Bring the files main added into line with the tickets so the "done when" conditions still hold: in A, migrate any local keyboard-dispatch, App-mount and settle helpers in the new files to the shared helpers (same rule as before: preserve each test's dispatch target exactly) and check the new files for real-timer waits of the kind Ticket 8 removed; in B, move the new files into the feature folders and fix path references. tests/reminders.helpers.ts is a shared helper: place it under tests/support or the reminders folder, whichever matches your layout.
3. Re-baseline counts from main: record files/tests/skips on plain origin/main, and show the stack ends with the same number of test cases (default and rendered).
4. PR #34 (impeccable/account-first-run) is still open; refresh its touched-file list and keep deferring those paths.
5. Push all three and get CI green on #41 and #42. Run the default frontend suite once locally on C's final head and the rendered suite once (expect 33 passed and the one known overflow failure, unless main changed that); otherwise let CI carry the load. If main moves again before you finish, finish against the commit you started with and tell me; I will merge straight away and we handle anything newer as a small follow-up.
Report head SHAs, CI run URLs, the re-baselined counts, and the list of new files you migrated or moved. Still do not merge.
